body.translated_text: <s>Śrīpāda Dhyānacandra Gosvāmī</s>

body.text: sādhako brāhma-muhūrte cotthāya nijeṣṭa-nāmāni smaret kīrtayed vā--
body.translated_text: The practitioner, rising at the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (predawn hour), should remember or chant the names of his chosen deity—

children.translated_text: Victorious is he of pure valor,
Golden-hued, with lotus-wide eyes,
With beautiful arms reaching to his knees,
Who dances in manifold ways with the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).
"O <s>Śrī Rāma</s>! O <s>Janārdana</s>! O Lord of the worlds! O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!
O Blissful One! O Compassionate One! O Beloved of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)! O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!
Make me forever plunged in the waves and surges of the great nectar-ocean of the blessed Name,

children.text: muhyantaṃ galad-aśru-netram avaśaṃ māṃ nātha nityaṃ kuru || 2 ||
children.translated_text: Swooning, with tears streaming from my eyes, helpless—O Lord, make me thus always!"
"O Beloved of <s>Śrī</s>! O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O Compassionate One! O Lotus-naveled One!
O Beloved of <s>Kaivalya</s> (liberation)! O <s>Mukunda</s>! O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>!"—
This garland of Names, like a necklace of spotless pearls
That surpasses the beauty of <s>Lakṣmī</s>—may I place it upon my throat.

children.text: kṛṣṇa rāma mukunda vāmana vāsudeva jagadguro
children.translated_text: "O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, Teacher of the universe!

children.text: matsya kacchapa narasiṃha varāha rāghava pāhi mām /
children.translated_text: O Fish (<s>Matsya</s>), Tortoise (<s>Kacchapa</s>), Man-Lion (<s>Narasiṃha</s>), Boar (<s>Varāha</s>), <s>Rāghava</s>—protect me!
O you who are worshipped by gods, demons, <s>Nārada</s>, and the foremost sages! O Ocean of Compassion!

children.text: devakī-suta dehi me tava pāda-bhaktim acañcalām || 4 ||
children.translated_text: O Son of <s>Devakī</s>, grant me unwavering devotion to your feet!"

children.text: he gopālaka he kṛpā-jala-nidhe he sindhu-kanyā-pate
children.translated_text: "O Cowherd! O Ocean of the waters of mercy! O Lord of the Daughter of the Ocean!

children.text: he kaṃsāntaka he gajendra-karuṇā-pārīṇa he mādhava /
children.translated_text: O Slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>! O you who showed compassion to the Lord of Elephants (<s>Gajendra</s>)! O <s>Mādhava</s>!

children.text: he rāmānuja he jagattraya-guro he puṇḍarīkākṣa māṃ
children.translated_text: O Younger Brother of <s>Rāma</s>! O Teacher of the three worlds! O Lotus-eyed One!

children.text: he gopī-jana-nātha pālaya paraṃ jānāmi na tvāṃ vinā || 5 ||
children.translated_text: O Lord of the <s>Gopī</s> maidens, protect me! I know no one other than you."
"O <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>! O Lotus-eyed One! O <s>Śrī Rāma</s>! O Lord of <s>Sītā</s>!
O <s>Govinda</s>! O <s>Acyuta</s>! O Delight of <s>Nanda</s>! O <s>Mukunda</s>! O Blissful One! O <s>Dāmodara</s>!
O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! O <s>Rāghava</s>! O <s>Vāsudeva</s>! O Man-Lion! O Crest-jewel of the Lord of Gods!
O Helmsman across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>! O <s>Hari</s>! O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! Salutation to you!"
"O you adorned with a peacock-feather crown under the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> tree! O you whose limbs are anointed with fine sandalwood!
O Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>! O you who are dark like a radiant blue lotus!
O Beloved of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>)! O Delight of <s>Nanda</s>! O Supreme Bliss! O Lotus-eyed One!

children.text: śrī-govinda mukunda sundara-tano māṃ dīnam ānandaya || 7 ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrī Govinda</s>! O <s>Mukunda</s>! O you of beautiful form—give joy to wretched me!"

body.translated_text: (<s>Padyāvalī</s> 33-38)

children.translated_text: "O Goddess, girdled by the ocean, whose breasts are the mountains!

children.text: viṣṇu-patni namas tubhyaṃ pāda-sparśaṃ kṣamasva me || 8 ||
children.translated_text: O Consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, salutation to you! Forgive the touch of my feet."

body.text: tato bahir gatvā maitra-kṛtyādi-vidhiṃ kuryāt, danta-dhāvanādim ācaret, śuddhaāsane pūrvābhimukhī upaviśya niścala-manāḥ -
body.translated_text: Then, going outside, one should perform the morning duties such as evacuation, tooth-cleaning, and so forth. Sitting on a clean seat facing east, with a steady mind—

children.text: smaret śrīmad gaura-candraṃ svardhunyā dakṣiṇe taṭe /
children.translated_text: One should remember the blessed <s>Gauracandra</s> (golden moon) on the southern bank of the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>),
In the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) abode named <s>Śrī Navadvīpa</s>.
On the beautiful bank of the celestial river, with a form resembling a great tortoise's back shining forth,
Surrounded by lovely gardens, encircled by great mansions of jewels and gold,
Where eternally before every house arises the drama of <s>Kṛṣṇa saṃkīrtana</s> overflowing with love—

children.text: śrī-vṛndāṭavy abhinnaṃ tri-jagad anupamaṃ śrī-navadvīpam īḍe || 10 ||
children.translated_text: I praise <s>Śrī Navadvīpa</s>, inseparable from <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, incomparable in the three worlds.
With banks shining with blossoming trees, creepers, and tender shoots, with rows of waves,
Beautiful with gentle breezes, swans, and lotuses, where bees alight upon lotus clusters,
With multitudes of divine <s>tīrthas</s> (holy places) studded with precious gems, her body dusted
With the dust of the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Gaura</s>—such is the holy <s>Gaṅgā</s>, most purifying.
In the midst of that most beautiful golden celestial river,

children.text: dvīpo bhāti sumaṅgalo madhu-ripor ānanda-vanyo mahān /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Navadvīpa</s> shines, most auspicious, the great blissful grove of the Enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),
Delightful with various trees and creepers laden with flowers and fruits, greatly frequented,
Captivating to the heart and ears with the calls of birds of various colors.
The trunks are of emerald, the branches of abundant trees are of gold,
The rows of leaves are of soft ruby, the buds are of coral,
The clusters of flowers are of fine diamond, the rows of fruits

children.text: śreṇī yasya sa ko 'pi śākhi-nikaro yatrātimātrojjvalaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: Are of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl)—such is the incomparable grove of trees, resplendent beyond measure.
In its midst, the city with beautiful courtyards of homes of multitudes of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and good people,
With gardens, orchards, and shining platforms as places of recreation,
Eternally festive with great devotees resplendent with the power of true <s>bhakti</s>,
Where in every home a great image of the Enemy of Sin (<s>Hari</s>) shines—such is this city.

body.text: evaṃbhūte śrī-navadvīpa-madhye manasi nivāsaṃ kṛtvā tatra śrī-gurudevasya śayyotthāna-mukha-prakṣālana-danta-dhāvanādi-krameṇa yathā-yogyaṃ sevāṃ kuryāt sevānantaraṃ dhyāyet yathā yāmale--
body.translated_text: Having thus mentally established one's residence in the midst of <s>Śrī Navadvīpa</s>, one should serve the blessed <s>Gurudeva</s> in proper sequence—his rising from bed, face-washing, tooth-cleaning, and so forth. After the service, one should meditate as stated in the <s>Yāmala</s>—
Now the meditation on <s>Śrī Guru</s>—

children.translated_text: I remember the <s>Guru</s>, whose lotus feet drip with the honey of compassion,
Who wears white garments, whose complexion is golden, who is eternal,
Who is gracious, adorned with fine garlands and ornaments, a treasury of virtues—
I remember that true devotee, the <s>Guru</s>, who is <s>Hari</s> [himself].

body.text:
śrī-guru-parama-guru-parātpara-guru-parameṣṭhi-gurūṇām anugāmitvena śrīman mahāprabhor mandiraṃ gacchet /
tatra tad-ājñayā śrī-navadvīpa-candrasya śayyotthānaṃ suvāsita-jalena śrī-mukha-prakṣālanādi-krameṇa sevāṃ kuryāt /
body.translated_text:
Following in succession the <s>Śrī Guru</s>, the <s>Parama-guru</s>, the <s>Parātpara-guru</s>, and the <s>Parameṣṭhi-guru</s>, one should go to the temple of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s>.
There, by his command, one should serve <s>Śrī Navadvīpa-candra</s> in sequence: his rising from bed, washing of his blessed face with fragrant water, and so forth.

body.text: tatra śrīman mahāprabhor dhyānaṃ yathā ūrddhvāmnāye (3.15)--
body.translated_text: Now the meditation on <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s> as stated in the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya</s> (3.15)—

children.translated_text: Two-armed, beautiful as gold, with hands [showing the gestures of] boon-granting and fearlessness,
Embracing with loving arms, chanting the name of <s>Hari</s>.

body.translated_text: Next one should meditate on <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>—

children.translated_text: "<s>Vṛndāvana</s>, surrounded by divine creepers,
The creepers bearing clusters of blossoming flowers,
The flowers abounding with intoxicated bees,
The bees singing songs that steal the ears."
"In the midst of beautiful <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, adorned with fifty groves,
In a bower of wish-fulfilling trees, in a house made of divine jewels—"

body.text: tatra siddha-dehena śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇayor niśānta-līlāṃ smared yathā--
body.translated_text: There, in one's perfected spiritual body, one should remember the late-night <s>līlā</s> (divine play) of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as follows—

body.text:
niśāvasāne śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇau śrī-vṛndā-niyukta-rasamaya-parama-vidagdha-śuka-śāri-vṛnda-padya-paṭhana-janita-prabodhāv api gāḍhopagūhana-sukha-bhaṅgād asahiṣṇutayā kṣaṇam avakāśyamāna-jāgarau tat-tat-padya-prapaṭhita-niśāvasāna-sātaṅkau puṣpamayānanda-talpotthitau sva-sva-kuñjāt tat-kālāgata-śrīmal-lalitā-viśākhādi-priya-sakhī-vṛnda-sanarma-vāg-vilāsena sāntarānandau kakkhaṭy-udita-jaṭilā-śravaṇāt sa-śaṅkau saṅga-tyāga-bhayam
asahamānau tau bhītyotkaṇṭhākulau sva-sva-gṛhaṃ gacchataḥ /
body.translated_text: At the end of the night, <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though awakened by the recitation of poems by supremely artful parrots and <s>śārī</s> birds full of <s>rasa</s>, appointed by <s>Śrī Vṛndā</s>, yet unable to bear the breaking of the happiness of their tight embrace, allowing wakefulness only for a moment, alarmed by the approaching end of night proclaimed in those very poems, arise from their blissful flower-bed, and from their own bower, [attended by] <s>Śrīmat Lalitā</s> arriving at that hour—

body.text:
evaṃ krameṇa śrī-gauracandrasya śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇayor līlāṃ smaret /
niśānta-līlā-smaraṇānantaraṃ gurv-ādīn daṇḍavat praṇamet yathā--
body.translated_text:
In this sequence one should remember the <s>līlās</s> of <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s> and <s>Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa</s>.
After remembering the late-night <s>līlā</s>, one should offer prostrations to the <s>Guru</s> and others, as follows—

children.translated_text: "Of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance,

children.text: cakṣur unmīlitaṃ yena tasmai śrī-gurave namaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: Whose eyes were opened by the collyrium-stick of knowledge—salutation to that blessed <s>Guru</s>."

body.text:
iti mantraṃ paṭhitvā śrī-guruṃ daṇḍavat praśamya evaṃ parama-guru-parātpara-guru-parameṣṭhi-guru-gosvāmi-caraṇān krameṇa daṇḍavat praṇamet /
tataḥ śrī-gauracandraṃ praṇamet--
body.translated_text:
Having recited this <s>mantra</s>, one should prostrate fully before <s>Śrī Guru</s>, and then in sequence prostrate fully before the <s>Parama-guru</s>, <s>Parātpara-guru</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhi-guru</s>, and the <s>Gosvāmī</s> masters.
Then one should bow to <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s>—

children.translated_text: "Salutation, salutation to <s>Viśvambhara</s>, to <s>Gaura</s>, to <s>Caitanya</s>, the Great Soul,
To the Son of <s>Śacī</s>, to the Friend, to the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>!"
"I worship <s>Nityānanda</s>, with a pearl hanging from his ear,
Who in the form of <s>Caitanya</s>'s elder brother has purified the earth."
"He who has delivered all people, the compassionate one,
Whose mind is immersed in the ocean of the nectar of <s>prema</s> (love),
Who is honored and worshipped by <s>Caitanyacandra</s>—
I bow my head to that <s>Advaitacandra</s>."

children.text: gadādhara namas tubhyaṃ yasya gaurāṅgo jīvanam /
children.translated_text: "Salutation to you, <s>Gadādhara</s>, for whom <s>Gaurāṅga</s> is life itself!
Salutation to you, <s>Śrī Śrīnivāsa Paṇḍita</s>, embodiment of <s>prema</s>!"

body.translated_text: In this sequence one should prostrate fully before the assembly of <s>Gaura</s>'s devotees.

body.text:
śrī-navadvīpa-dhāmne namaḥ /
śrī-gaṅgāyai namaḥ /
śrī-saṅkīrtanāya namaḥ /
śrī-gauḍa-maṇḍalāya namaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Salutation to the holy abode of <s>Śrī Navadvīpa</s>!
Salutation to <s>Śrī Gaṅgā</s>!
Salutation to <s>Śrī Saṃkīrtana</s>!
Salutation to <s>Śrī Gauḍa-maṇḍala</s>!

children.translated_text: "Beautiful as ten million <s>Kandarpas</s> (Cupids), with the radiance of a shining blue lotus,
Salutation to the Son of the King of Cowherds (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), whose play enchants the universe!"
"O <s>Rādhā</s>, of golden limbs like molten gold, O Sovereign of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
O Daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, O Goddess, I bow to you, Beloved of <s>Hari</s>!"
"Equal to the very life of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>, her younger [attendant],
Trained in the arts of happiness by <s>Viśākhā</s>,
Whose limbs overflow with the nectar of the divine play's sweetness—
I bow to the <s>Mañjarī</s> named <s>Anaṅga</s> and others."

body.text:
lalitādi-parama-preṣṭha-sakhī-vṛndebhyo namaḥ /
kusumikādi-sakhī-vṛndebhyo namaḥ /
kastūryādi-nitya-sakhī-vṛndebhyo namaḥ /
śaśimukhyādi-prāṇa-sakhī-vṛndebhyo namaḥ /
kuraṅgākṣyādi-priya-sakhī-vṛndebhyo namaḥ /
śrī-rūpādi-mañjarībhyo namaḥ /
śrīdāmādi-sakhi-vṛndebhyo namaḥ /
sarva-gopa-gopībhyo namaḥ /
vraja-vāsibhyo namaḥ /
śrī-vṛndā-vipinebhyo namaḥ /
śrī-rāsa-maṇḍalāya namaḥ /
śrī-yamunāyai namaḥ /
śrī-rādhā-kuṇḍa-śyāma-kuṇḍābhyāṃ namaḥ /
śrī-govardhanāya namaḥ /
śrī-dvādaśa-vipinebhyo namaḥ /
śrī-vraja-maṇḍalāya namaḥ /
śrī-mathurā-maṇḍalāya namaḥ /
sarvāvatārebhyo namaḥ /
ananta-koṭi-vaiṣṇavebhyo namaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Salutation to the group of most beloved <s>sakhīs</s> (friends) headed by <s>Lalitā</s>!
Salutation to the group of <s>sakhīs</s> headed by <s>Kusumikā</s>!
Salutation to the group of eternal <s>sakhīs</s> headed by <s>Kastūrī</s>!
Salutation to the group of life-companions headed by <s>Śaśimukhī</s>!
Salutation to the group of dear <s>sakhīs</s> headed by <s>Kuraṅgākṣī</s>!
Salutation to the <s>Mañjarīs</s> headed by <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>!
Salutation to the group of friends headed by <s>Śrīdāmā</s>!
Salutation to all the <s>Gopas</s> and <s>Gopīs</s>!

children.translated_text: "To those who are wish-fulfilling trees, to those who are oceans of mercy,
To those who are the purifiers of the fallen—salutation, salutation to the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>!"

body.text: atha snānam ācaret yathā--nady ādau pravāhābhimukhe taḍāgādiṣu pūrvābhimukhī tīrthāni āhvayed yathā--
body.translated_text: Now one should perform the bath as follows—in a river or similar [body of water], facing the current, or in a tank facing east, one should invoke the sacred waters as follows—

children.text: gaṅge ca yamune caiva godāvari sarasvati /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O <s>Yamunā</s>, O <s>Godāvarī</s>, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: narmade sindho kāveri jale 'smin sannidhiṃ kuru || 28 ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Narmadā</s>, O <s>Sindhu</s>, O <s>Kāverī</s>—be present in this water!"
"O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, destroyer of great sins, O Compassionate One,
Shining on the head of the great Lord (<s>Śiva</s>), playing in the mind's delight,
O you who are the flowing <s>Brahman</s>-abode, born from the lotus-foot of the Imperishable One (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),
Purify me, O Daughter [of Heaven], O you rich in flowing waves!"

children.text: viṣṇor nābhy-ambu-madhyād vara-kamalam abhūt tasya nālī-sumeror
children.translated_text: "From the center of the navel-water of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, a beautiful lotus arose; from its stalk, [which is] <s>Sumeru</s>,

children.text: madhye niḥsyandamānā tvam asi bhagavati brahma-lokāt prasūtā /
children.translated_text: Flowing down, you are, O Blessed One, born from <s>Brahmaloka</s>;

children.text: khād-bhraṣṭā rudra-mūrdhni praṇipatita-jalā gāṃ gatāsīti gaṅgā
children.translated_text: Falling from the sky upon <s>Rudra</s>'s head, your waters prostrated, you came to the earth—O <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
Who would not worship you, purified by contact with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>?"

children.text: gaṅgā gaṅgeti yo brūyāt yojanānāṃ śatair api /
children.translated_text: "One who says '<s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' even from a distance of hundreds of <s>yojanas</s>,
Is freed from all sins and goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
"Of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sun of consciousness and bliss, the eternal Son of <s>Nanda</s>,
She is the supreme vessel of divine love, her body the flowing <s>Brahman</s>,
The remover of sins, the bestower of the world's welfare—
May she, the Daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), purify our bodies!"
"O you whose fortune equals that of <s>Rādhikā</s>, worshipped by all <s>tīrthas</s>,

children.text: prasīda rādhikā-kuṇḍa snāmi te salile śubhe || 33 ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious! O <s>Rādhikā-kuṇḍa</s>, I bathe in your auspicious waters."

body.text: tataḥ śukla-vastre paridhāya śrī-hari-mandira-dhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā śrī-hari-nāmākṣaram aṅkayed gātre--
body.translated_text: Then, putting on white garments and wearing the marks of <s>Śrī Hari</s>'s temple [on the body], one should inscribe the syllables of <s>Śrī Hari</s>'s names on the body—

children.translated_text: "One should meditate on <s>Keśava</s> on the forehead, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> on the belly,
<s>Mādhava</s> on the chest, and <s>Govinda</s> in the hollow of the throat.

children.text: viṣṇuṃ ca dakṣiṇe kukṣau bāhau ca madhusūdanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> on the right side of the belly, <s>Madhusūdana</s> on the [right] arm,
<s>Trivikrama</s> on the shoulder, <s>Vāmana</s> on the left side,

children.text: śrīdharaṃ vāma-bāhau tu hṛṣīkeśaṃ ca kandhare /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdhara</s> on the left arm, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> on the [left] shoulder,

children.text: pṛṣṭhe tu padma-nābhaṃ ca kaṭyāṃ dāmodaraṃ nyaset /
children.translated_text: <s>Padmanābha</s> on the back, and one should place <s>Dāmodara</s> on the waist;
The water from washing [the <s>tilaka</s> implements], [invoking] <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [is placed] on the head."

body.text: pūrvavat sthirāsane sthira-cittaḥ tatrādau śrī-navadvīpa-madhye śrī-ratna-mandire ratna-siṃhāsanopari bhakta-vṛnda-parisevitaṃ śrī-śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṃ gurvādi-krameṇa dhyātvā pūjayet /
body.translated_text: As before, seated firmly on a steady seat with a steady mind, first in the midst of <s>Śrī Navadvīpa</s>, in a jeweled temple upon a jeweled lion-throne, one should meditate upon and worship <s>Śrī Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Deva</s>, attended by a multitude of devotees, following the sequence of the <s>Guru</s> and others.

body.text:
tatrādau śrī-jagannātha-miśrasya mandiraṃ dhyāyet /
yathā caitanyārcana-candrikāyām--
body.translated_text:
First one should meditate on the temple of <s>Śrī Jagannātha Miśra</s>.
As stated in the <s>Caitanyārcanacandrikā</s>—

children.translated_text: "The courtyard of the temple of <s>Śrī Jagannātha Miśra</s>, with excellent
Wondrous temple-buildings adorned with various jewels and gems;
In its midst, a golden rampart whose splendor puts the sun to shame, with a gateway,
The house of <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>, with a courtyard for <s>saṃkīrtana</s> shining in front,
The inner quarters of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, with kitchen, dining hall, bedchamber, and a beautiful moon-terrace—
Such is the city of <s>Gaurāṅga Hari</s>, bestowing happiness, expanding with its own bliss."
"In its midst, [a temple] with nine pinnacles topped with jeweled vessels, within [walls of] the finest jewels,
With variegated golden panels strung with pearl garlands, studded with gems of true devotion,
With four Veda-doorways, eight polished gem-studded doors of splendid panels,
A temple adorned with moonstone canopies, ruby [ornaments], and hanging moon-jewels."
"In its midst, upon a throne of jewels and variegated gold, inscribed with <s>mantra</s>-syllable <s>yantras</s>,
Resembling the pistil and beautiful stamens atop the <s>karṇikāra</s> [flower] within a hexagon—"
Upon the splendor of the great, tortoise-shaped supreme <s>yoga</s>, upon the lotus of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> (seat of yoga),
stainless with the beauty of rows of moons and a hundred thousand suns, there shines a throne.
With pillars of emerald set upon lotus-petal bases on the sides below, with lapis lazuli backs,
with canopies of radiance bearing great pearls and excellent gems hanging from ornate coverings,
with cushions of cotton within Chinese silk cloth seats, soft as the moon at the edges and backs,
with marvelous <s>mantras</s> within gold, an eight-layered treasury accessible through meditation on the feet of Lord <s>Hari</s>.
In the middle of that, one should remember <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s>; on the left, the glorious <s>Gadādhara</s>;
on his right, the lord of <s>avadhūtas</s>, the glorious <s>Advaita</s>; then one should meditate.
On his right, one should remember <s>Śrīnivāsa</s> and the glorious foremost of <s>paṇḍitas</s>;
and one should remember the glorious assembly of devotees, well-arranged in the four directions.
Among the glorious assembly of <s>Gaura</s>'s devotees, each accompanied by their own followers,
beginning with <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Svarūpa</s>, one should remember the <s>gurus</s> situated among their own groups.

body.translated_text: First, the remembrance of <s>Śrī Guru</s>, as stated in the <s>Sanat-kumāra Saṃhitā</s>:

children.translated_text: Resplendent like ten thousand moons, with hands shining with the gestures of boon-granting and fearlessness,
wearing white garments, with divine white garlands and unguents,
of cheerful countenance, peaceful, blissful in the joy of <s>bhajana</s> (devotional worship),
bearing a divine form—one should meditate on him as boon-granting and lotus-eyed.
Eager in service, having approached the lineage of <s>gurus</s> beginning with <s>Rūpa</s>,

children.text: evaṃ rūpaṃ guruṃ dhyāyen manasā sādhakaḥ śuciḥ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: the pure practitioner should meditate on the <s>guru</s> of such form with the mind.

body.translated_text: Near him, one should visualize oneself as eager for service, as follows:

children.translated_text: With forehead adorned with the divine tilaka of <s>Śrī Hari</s>'s temple, neck beautiful with a garland,
chest adorned with the letters of <s>Śrī Hari</s>'s name, anointed again with sandalwood paste,

children.text: śuddhaṃ śubhra-navāmbaraṃ vimalatāṃ nityaṃ vahantīṃ tanuṃ
children.translated_text: pure, wearing fresh white garments, a body ever bearing purity—
one should meditate on oneself as eager for service near the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Guru</s>.
With hair bound by a beautiful pearl garland, with a face smiling like the moon,
with charming, variegated garments of sandalwood and <s>aguru</s>, adorned with divine garlands and ornaments,
sweet with the delight and rapture of the mood of dance, radiant in the attire of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love),
I worship <s>Caitanya</s>, of golden splendor, being served by his own people.
With beautiful gait that shames the king of elephants, with sacred feet, with dark garment
resembling a row of blue lotuses, with bodily radiance rivaling the twilight moon,
with eyes like intoxicated <s>khañjana</s> birds rolling in the surge of love, with laughing face—
I constantly remember <s>Nityānanda</s>, whose limbs are radiant with ornaments.
With lotus feet attended by hosts of true devotees, wearing garments white as <s>kunda</s> flowers and the moon,
with the luster of pure gold, with beautiful twin arms, with a smiling, beautiful face,
with the gaze of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>, with hands granting boons and fearlessness, adorned with ornaments of <s>prema</s> (divine love)—
I constantly remember <s>Advaita</s>, the Lord, the sole root of supreme bliss.
With lotus feet that are the sole nectar of compassion, with the radiance of <s>Caitanya</s>-moon,
with right hand in the gesture of offering <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), wearing white garments, most excellent,
with a body of <s>premānanda</s> (bliss of divine love), with a face of nectarean smile, with the gaze of <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s>—
one should meditate on the glorious <s>Gadādhara</s>, the best of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, radiant with the ornament of sweetness.
Those who drink the honey of the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>, radiant with the ornament of pure <s>prema</s>,
with the luster of pure gold, with bodily beauty of tears, horripilation, and perspiration,
with offerings of service in their hands, with smiling faces, in white garments, most excellent—
let us meditate on those blissful associates, the great souls <s>Śrīvāsa</s> and others.

body.text:
iti smaraṇānantaraṃ śrī-guror ājñayā śrīman-mahāprabhuṃ ṣoḍaśopacārādibhiḥ tan-mūla-mantreṇaiva pūjayet /
śrīman-mahāprabhu-mantroddhāro yathā ūrddhvāmnāye śrī-vyāsaṃ prati śrī-nārada-vākyam (3.14-16)
body.translated_text:
After this remembrance, by the command of <s>Śrī Guru</s>, one should worship <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s> with sixteen offerings and the like, using his root <s>mantra</s> alone.
The extraction of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s>'s <s>mantra</s>, as stated by <s>Śrī Nārada</s> to <s>Śrī Vyāsa</s> in the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya</s> (3.14-16):

children.translated_text: O, a most secret question has been put forth by you;

children.text: mantraṃ vakṣyāmi te brahman mahā-puṇya-pradaṃ śubham || 54 ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you the <s>mantra</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, bestowing great merit, auspicious.

children.text: klīṃ gaurāya nama iti sarva-lokeṣu pūjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Klīṃ gaurāya namaḥ</s>'—this is worshiped in all worlds.
Worshiped with the seed-syllables of <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Anaṅga</s>, and the <s>vāg-bīja</s> (speech-seed),
this six-syllabled one is proclaimed as the king of <s>mantras</s>, a wish-fulfilling tree of the gods.

body.text: mantro yathā--kliṃ gaurāya namaḥ; hrīṃ, śrīṃ, klīṃ, aiṃ gaurāya namaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is as follows: <s>Klīṃ gaurāya namaḥ</s>; <s>Hrīṃ, Śrīṃ, Klīṃ, Aiṃ gaurāya namaḥ</s>.

body.text: etat pādyam, etad arghyam, etad ācamanīyam, eṣa gandhaḥ, etat puṣpam, eṣa dhūpaḥ, eṣa dīpaḥ, etan naivedyam, etat pānīya-jalam, idam ācamanīyam, etat tāmbūlam, etad gandha-mālyam, eṣa puṣpāñjalir ityādi /
body.translated_text: This is the <s>pādya</s> (foot-water), this is the <s>arghya</s> (respectful offering), this is the <s>ācamanīya</s> (mouth-rinsing water), this is the <s>gandha</s> (fragrance), this is the <s>puṣpa</s> (flower), this is the <s>dhūpa</s> (incense), this is the <s>dīpa</s> (lamp), this is the <s>naivedya</s> (food offering), this is the drinking water, this is the <s>ācamanīya</s>, this is the <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), this is the <s>gandha-mālya</s> (fragrant garland), this is the offering of flowers, and so forth.

body.text: evaṃ śrī-nityānanda-prabhuṃ pūjayet, śrīman-nityānanda-prabhor mantroddhāro yathā (brahmāṇḍa-purāṇe dharaṇī-śeṣa-samvāde)--
body.translated_text: In the same way, one should worship <s>Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu</s>. The extraction of <s>Śrīman Nityānanda Prabhu</s>'s <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> (in the dialogue of <s>Dharaṇī</s> and <s>Śeṣa</s>):

children.translated_text: Listen! This <s>mantra</s> consisting of one hundred and eight names has been offered to you.

children.text: mayā tvayi purā proktaṃ kāma-bījeti saṃjñakam || 56 ||
children.translated_text: It was formerly told to you by me, known as the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (desire-seed).

children.text: vahni-bījena pūtānte cādau deva namas tathā /
children.translated_text: Purified by the <s>vahni-bīja</s> (fire-seed) at the end, with 'O deity, obeisance' at the beginning,
the word '<s>Jāhnavī</s>' is placed there, then 'to the beloved' after that.
This twelve-syllabled <s>mantra</s> is captivating everywhere.

body.text:
mantro yathā--kliṃ deva-jāhnavī-vallabhāya svāhā /
iti mantreṇaiva pūjayet /
body.translated_text:
The <s>mantra</s> is as follows: <s>Klīṃ deva-jāhnavī-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.
One should worship with this very <s>mantra</s>.

body.text:
evaṃ śrī-advaita-prabhuṃ pūjayet /
atha śrī-advaita-prabhor mantroddhāro yathā pādme--
body.translated_text:
In the same way, one should worship <s>Śrī Advaita Prabhu</s>.
Now the extraction of <s>Śrī Advaita Prabhu</s>'s <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: O <s>Nārada</s>, best of sages, a most secret question!

children.text: na prakāśyas tvayā hy etad guhyād guhyataraṃ mahat || 58 ||
children.translated_text: This, which is the greatest of secrets, should not be revealed by you.
Endowed with the <s>kāma-bīja</s>, with <s>Advaita</s> and the <s>vahni-nāyikā</s> (fire-consort),
ending in <s>ṅe</s>—this <s>mantra</s> of the <s>ṛṣi</s>-syllables is most difficult to obtain.

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is as follows: <s>Klīṃ advaitāya svāhā</s>.

body.text: tad-anantaraṃ śrīman-mahāprabhoḥ śeṣa-nirmālyena śrī-gadādhara-paṇḍitaṃ pūjayet tan-mantreṇaiva, śrī-gadādhara-paṇḍita-mantro yathā--śrīṃ gadādharāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: After that, with the remaining <s>nirmālya</s> (sacred remnants) of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s>, one should worship <s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> with his own <s>mantra</s>. <s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s>'s <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ gadādharāya svāhā</s>.

body.text: atha tathaiva śrī-śrīvāsādi-bhaktān guru-vargādīn mahāprabhu-nirmālya-prasādena pūjayet, sva-sva-nāma-caturthyantena śrī-guru-devaṃ tu tan-mūla-mantreṇaiva pūjayet /
body.translated_text: Then, in the same way, one should worship the devotees such as <s>Śrī Śrīvāsa</s> and the lineage of <s>gurus</s> with the <s>prasāda</s> (sacred remnants) of <s>Mahāprabhu</s>'s <s>nirmālya</s>, using the dative form of each one's own name. But <s>Śrī Gurudeva</s> should be worshiped with his own root <s>mantra</s>.
The extraction of <s>Śrī Guru</s>'s <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Bṛhad-brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> (in the dialogue of <s>Sūta</s> and <s>Śaunaka</s>):

children.text: śrīṃ gum ity eva bhagavad-gurave vahni-vallabhā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrīṃ guṃ</s>'—thus, to the divine <s>guru</s>, with the <s>vahni-vallabhā</s> (beloved of fire),
this ten-syllabled king of <s>mantras</s> is the protector in all activities.

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is as follows: <s>Śrīṃ guṃ bhagavad-gurave svāhā</s>.

body.text:
tato 'vaśeṣa-nirmālyādikaṃ gṛhṇīyāt; sthānāntare ca saṃsthāpya prabhupāda-padme puṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā ārātrikaṃ kuryāt /
tad-antaraṃ cāmara-vyajanādikaṃ kṛtvā śrī-guru-pārśve tiṣṭhan dhyānānukrameṇa nirīkṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tato bahiḥ-pūjayet /
bahiḥ-pūjāṃ kṛtvānantaraṃ sva-sva-gāyatrī-mantrān japet kramāt--
body.translated_text:
Then one should receive the remaining <s>nirmālya</s> and other articles; and having established them in another place and having offered a handful of flowers at the lotus feet of <s>Prabhu</s>, one should perform <s>ārātrika</s> (lamp-waving ceremony).
After that, having performed fanning with the <s>cāmara</s> (yak-tail fan) and the like, standing beside <s>Śrī Guru</s>, having looked upon the deity following the order of meditation, one should then perform external worship.
Having performed external worship, one should then recite the respective <s>Gāyatrī mantras</s> in order:

body.text: tatrādau śrī-guru-gāyatrī yathā pādme--śrīṃ gurudevāya vidmahe gaura-priyāya dhīmahi tan no guruḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text: First, <s>Śrī Guru Gāyatrī</s> as stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>: '<s>Śrīṃ gurudevāya vidmahe gaura-priyāya dhīmahi tan no guruḥ pracodayāt</s>.'

children.text: prathamaṃ mantra-guroḥ pūjā paścāc caiva mamārcanam /
children.translated_text: First is the worship of the <s>mantra-guru</s>, and afterward is my worship;

children.text: kurvan siddhim avāpnoti hy anyathā niṣphalaṃ bhavet || 61 ||
children.translated_text: performing thus, one attains perfection; otherwise it is fruitless.

children.text: dhyānādau śrī-guror mūrtiṃ pūjādau ca guroḥ pūjām /
children.translated_text: In meditation, the form of <s>Śrī Guru</s> first; in worship, the worship of <s>Guru</s> first;

children.text: japādau ca guror mantraṃ hy anyathā niṣphalaṃ bhavet || 62 ||
children.translated_text: in <s>japa</s> (recitation), the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Guru</s> first; otherwise it is fruitless.

body.translated_text: Then the characteristics of <s>japa</s>, as stated (<s>Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> 17.143, 129):

children.text: na kampayec chiro grīvāṃ dantān naiva prakāśayet /
children.translated_text: One should not shake the head or neck, nor should one show the teeth;
withdrawal of the mind, purity, silence, and contemplation of the meaning of the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: mano-madhye sthito mantro mantra-madhye sthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is situated within the mind, and the mind is situated within the <s>mantra</s>;
when mind and <s>mantra</s> are united—this indeed is the characteristic of <s>japa</s>.

body.translated_text: Now the rules regarding the fingers and so forth for <s>japa</s> (<s>Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> 17.116-120):

children.translated_text: When performing <s>japa</s> on the fingers, one should count with the thumb and fingers;

children.text: aṅguṣṭhena vinā karma kṛtas tad aphalaṃ bhavet || 65 ||
children.translated_text: an act done without the thumb becomes fruitless.
The little finger, ring finger, middle finger, and fourth is the index finger;
the three fingers each have three joints, while the middle finger has one joint.
One should avoid the two joints of the middle finger during the time of <s>japa</s>;

children.text: evaṃ meruṃ vijānīyād brahmaṇā dūṣitaṃ svayam || 67 ||
children.translated_text: thus one should understand the <s>meru</s> (summit-bead), declared as forbidden by <s>Brahmā</s> himself.
Beginning from the middle of the ring finger, proceeding clockwise in order,
up to the base of the index finger, through the ten joints in sequence.

children.text: aṅgulir na viyuñjīta kiñcit saṅkocayet talam /
children.translated_text: One should not separate the fingers; one should slightly contract the palm;

children.text: aṅgulīnāṃ viyoge tu chidreṣu sravate japaḥ || 69 ||
children.translated_text: if the fingers are separated, the <s>japa</s> leaks through the gaps.

body.text: madhyamā caika-parvikā ity ukteḥ kecit madhyamā-madhya-parva gṛhṇanti tan na /
body.translated_text: As stated 'the middle finger has one joint,' some take it to mean the middle joint of the middle finger—that is incorrect.
Now the order of <s>japa</s> is as follows:

children.translated_text: First, one should recite the <s>mantra-gāyatrī</s> of <s>Gurudeva</s>;
then the recitation of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s>;
one should recite the <s>mantra-gāyatrī</s> of the glorious Lord of <s>avadhūtas</s>, <s>Advaita</s>;
then of <s>Śrī Gadādhara</s> and of <s>Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita</s>.

body.text:
śrī-gurudevasya mantro yathā--śrīṃ guṃ bhagavad-gurave svāhā /
atha gāyatrī--śrīṃ gurudevāya vidmahe, gaura-priyāya dhīmahi, tan no guruḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text:
The <s>mantra</s> of <s>Śrī Gurudeva</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ guṃ bhagavad-gurave svāhā</s>.
And the <s>Gāyatrī</s>: <s>Śrīṃ gurudevāya vidmahe, gaura-priyāya dhīmahi, tan no guruḥ pracodayāt</s>.

body.text:
iti śrī-guru-gāyatrī-smaraṇānantaraṃ guru-vargān smaret; smaraṇa-kramo yathā--
śrī-guru-parama-gurur ityādi-krameṇa sva-sva-praṇāly-anusāreṇa sva-sva-parivāreśvara-parama-parameṣṭhi-guru-paryantaṃ dhyānaṃ kṛtvā svīya-svīya-nāmāni caturthyantaṃ kṛtvā japānantaraṃ śrī-śrī-caitanya-mahāprabhor mantraṃ gāyatrīṃ ca smaret /
body.translated_text:
After the remembrance of <s>Śrī Guru Gāyatrī</s>, one should remember the lineage of <s>gurus</s>. The order of remembrance is as follows:
In the order of <s>Śrī Guru</s>, <s>Parama-guru</s> (grand-preceptor), and so on, following the succession of one's own lineage, having meditated up to one's own respective lord, the supreme and supremely exalted <s>guru</s>, together with their retinues, and having formed their respective names in the dative case, after <s>japa</s>, one should then remember the <s>mantra</s> and <s>Gāyatrī</s> of <s>Śrī Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s>.

body.text:
mantro yathā -klīṃ gaurāya svāhā /
gāyatrī yathā -klīṃ caitanyāya vidmahe viśvambharāya dhīmahi tan no gauraḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text:
The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Klīṃ gaurāya svāhā</s>.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is: <s>Klīṃ caitanyāya vidmahe viśvambharāya dhīmahi tan no gauraḥ pracodayāt</s>.

body.text:
mantro yathā -klīṃ deva-jāhnavī-vallabhāya svāhā /
gāyatrī yathā -klīṃ nityānandāya vidmahe saṅkarṣaṇāya dhīmahi tan no balaḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text:
The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Klīṃ deva-jāhnavī-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is: <s>Klīṃ nityānandāya vidmahe saṅkarṣaṇāya dhīmahi tan no balaḥ pracodayāt</s>.

body.text:
mantro yathā -klīṃ advaitāya svāhā /
gāyatrī yathā -klīṃ advaitāya vidmahe mahā-viṣṇave dhīmahi tan no advaitaḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text:
The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Klīṃ advaitāya svāhā</s>.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is: <s>Klīṃ advaitāya vidmahe mahā-viṣṇave dhīmahi tan no advaitaḥ pracodayāt</s>.

body.text:
mantro yathā -śrīṃ gadādharāya svāhā /
gāyatrī yathā -gāṃ gadādharāya vidmahe paṇḍitākhyāya dhīmahi tan no gadādharaḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text:
The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ gadādharāya svāhā</s>.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is: <s>Gāṃ gadādharāya vidmahe paṇḍitākhyāya dhīmahi tan no gadādharaḥ pracodayāt</s>.

body.text:
mantro yathā -śrīṃ śrīvāsāya svāhā /
gāyatrī yathā -śrīṃ śrīvāsāya vidmahe nāradākhyāya dhīmahi tan no bhaktaḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text:
The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ śrīvāsāya svāhā</s>.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ śrīvāsāya vidmahe nāradākhyāya dhīmahi tan no bhaktaḥ pracodayāt</s>.

body.text: śrī śrī gaura-gadādhara mantro yathā -klīṃ śrīṃ gaura-gadādharāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> of <s>Śrī Śrī Gaura-Gadādhara</s> is: <s>Klīṃ śrīṃ gaura-gadādharāya svāhā</s>.
After performing prayers and obeisances, one should remember according to the outline of the eight daily periods of <s>Śrī Gauracandra</s>:

children.translated_text: From the rising of <s>Gaura</s> from sleep until his sleeping again,
the practitioner should perform service with various paraphernalia during those periods.
The wondrous nectar of the activities of <s>Śrī Navadvīpa-candra</s> (the moon of Navadvīpa)—
one should contemplate and contemplate it constantly, eager for mental service.
At the end of night, the sleeping of <s>Gauracandra</s> in his own abode;
in the morning, his rising, bathing, eating, and the like.
In the forenoon, his supreme eagerness in the devotees' temple;
at midday, wondrous pastimes on the bank of the celestial river.
In the afternoon, his wandering through <s>Navadvīpa</s>, full of great delight;
in the evening, his beautiful and splendid return to his own temple.
At dusk, in the home of <s>Śrīvāsa</s>, rich with his beloved companions;
at night, one should remember the blissful festival of glorious <s>saṃkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting).

body.text:
evaṃ śrī-caitanya-devaṃ niṣevya siddha-dehena śrī-kṛṣṇa-sevāṅgaṃ vidadhyāt /
atra kārikā--
body.translated_text:
Having thus served <s>Śrī Caitanyadeva</s>, one should perform the limb of service to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> with the <s>siddha-deha</s> (perfected spiritual body).
Here are the verses:

children.translated_text: At the time of contemplation and the like, one should perform it in accordance with that;

children.text: cintanaṃ tu tayos tatra vasan guru-gaṇānvitaḥ || 78 ||
children.translated_text: and the contemplation of those two should be done there, dwelling with the assembly of <s>gurus</s>.
Furthermore, in this <s>ākṣuṣa-līlā</s> (manifested pastimes), the practitioner with the <s>siddha-deha</s>
should mentally perform mental service appropriate to the eight daily periods.
The practitioner, with the <s>siddha-deha</s>, should serve in the abode of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s beloved,
near the beloved who has the form of one's <s>guru</s>, among the group of <s>sakhīs</s> (female companions) led by <s>Lalitā</s>.
One should always dwell in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>, accompanied by the <s>sakhī</s> who has the form of one's <s>guru</s>,
in the beautiful city of <s>Yāvaṭa</s> and also in the city of <s>Śrīmad Vṛṣabhānu</s>,
in the city of <s>Nandīśvara</s>, on both banks of <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa</s>,
in the delightful <s>Śrīmad Vṛndāvana</s>, of the lord and lady of <s>Śrīmad Vṛndāvana</s>.

children.text: prātar ādyaṣṭa-samaye sevanaṃ tu krameṇa ca /
children.translated_text: In the morning, at the first of the eight periods, service is performed in order.
With various divine accessories, foods and delicacies always,
with <s>cāmaras</s> (flywhisks), fans, and the like, and with foot-massaging and such services, (GGS 83)
a youthful <s>gopī</s> maiden, adorned with all ornaments,
with a pair of broad, elevated breasts, endowed with sixty-four arts, (GGS 84)
of hidden love (<s>bhāva</s>) toward <s>Govinda</s>, enchanting with the bliss of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma),
graced with the charm of discourse in various <s>rasas</s>, of divine form, (GGS 85)
filled with the abundance of <s>bhāva</s>-ecstasy born from the <s>rasa</s> of music,
day and night in her mind, both [Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa] agitated with an abundance of love, (GGS 86)
endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with <s>bhāva</s>, <s>hāva</s> (coquetry), and other expressions,
the source of the <s>guru</s>'s grace, a follower of the <s>guru</s>'s beloved form,
belonging to the <s>gāndharvikā</s> group, in her own group, accompanied by <s>Lalitā</s> and other associates. (GGS 87)
Following her own group-leader (<s>yūtheśvarī</s>), residing in the village of <s>Yāvaṭa</s>,
her form to be contemplated, following <s>Kāmarūpā</s>. (GGS 88)
Composed of the <s>rasa</s> of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>), of the radiance of molten gold,
dressed in fine blue garments, adorned with various ornaments, (GGS 89)
standing beside <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in the bloom of youth.
Her name is given by the <s>guru</s>; her mother is [named with the letters] of the first consonant-group plus <s>Mañjarī</s>;
her father is named with the third [consonant-group], and her husband is named with the last [consonant-group]. (GGS 90)

children.text: nivāso yāvaṭe tasyā dakṣiṇā mṛdvikā hi sā /
children.translated_text: Her residence is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>; she is gentle and of the right-wing (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) [temperament].
She is enriched with the service of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>'s garments, adorned with various ornaments. (GGS 91)
The practices (<s>sādhanas</s>) for this very <s>siddha-deha</s> (perfected body),
eleven well-known [items], are set forth in sequence, most enchanting. (GGS 92)

children.text: nāma rūpaṃ vayo veśaḥ sambandho yūtha eva ca /
children.translated_text: Name, form, age, dress, relationship, group,
command, service, supreme excellence, maidservant-to-be-protected, and residence. (GGS 93)

body.translated_text: The specific characteristics of these are stated:

children.translated_text: In accordance with one's name-designation, such as <s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s> and so on,
one should contemplate one's own name, appropriate for the beautiful-browed maidens of <s>Vraja</s>. (GGS 94)
The form should be carefully visualized as resembling the form of one's group-leader (<s>yūtheśvarī</s>),
enchanting to the three worlds, igniting desire in the Lord of the <s>gopīs</s>. (GGS 95)

children.text: vayo nānā-vidhaṃ tatra yat tu tridaśa-vatsaram /
children.translated_text: Age is of various kinds; that which is thirteen years,
the wonderfully sweet adolescence, is renowned among the beautiful-browed maidens of <s>Vraja</s>. (GGS 96)
Dress, with blue cloth and various ornaments,
suited to one's own body, naturally beautiful with <s>rasa</s>. (GGS 97)
The relationship of served and servant, according to the disposition of one's own mind—
one should never change that relationship, even at the cost of one's life. (GGS 98)
Just as the <s>yūtheśvarī</s>'s group always remains under her authority,
so too one should remain in every way under her control. (GGS 99)
Receiving the command of the <s>yūtheśvarī</s> upon one's head, one should perform
appropriate service to <s>Hari</s> and <s>Rādhā</s>, endowed with bliss. (GGS 100)
Attending to <s>cāmaras</s>, fans, and the like, carrying out all commands—
this should be understood as service, according to one's understanding, in its various aspects. (GGS 101)
Just as <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> and others have attained

children.text: prāpta nitya-sakhītvaṃ ca tathā syām iti bhāvayet || 102 ||
children.translated_text: the status of eternal companions (<s>nitya-sakhīs</s>) of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, so one should meditate: 'May I become likewise.' (GGS 102)

children.text: pālya-dāsī ca sā proktā paripālyā priyaṃvadā /
children.translated_text: The maidservant-to-be-protected is she who is to be nurtured, who speaks sweetly,
who, in the form of one's own mental disposition, is an eternal attendant. (GGS 103)
The residence is in the midst of <s>Vraja</s>, considered the abode of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—
<s>Vaṃśī-vaṭa</s> (the banyan of the flute) and <s>Śrī Nandīśvara</s>, which inspire great wonder. (GGS 104)
<s>Anaṅga Mañjarī</s>, <s>Vilāsa Mañjarī</s>,
<s>Aśoka Mañjarī</s>, and <s>Rasa Mañjarikā</s>, (GGS 105)
<s>Rasāla Mañjarī</s> by name, and <s>Kamala Mañjarī</s>,
the renowned <s>Karuṇā Mañjarī</s>, and the famous <s>Guṇa Mañjarī</s>— (GGS 106)

children.text: evaṃ sarvāś ca vikhyātāḥ sva-sva-nāmākṣaraiḥ parāḥ /
children.translated_text: thus all [the <s>mañjarīs</s>] are renowned by the syllables of their own names, supreme,
<s>mañjarīs</s> numerous, endowed with beauty, qualities, character, and youth. (GGS 107)

children.text: nāma-rūpādi tat sarvaṃ guru-dattaṃ ca bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: Name, form, and all the rest—given by the <s>guru</s>—one should meditate upon.

children.text: tatra tatra sthitā nityaṃ bhajet śrī-rādhikā-harī || 108 ||
children.translated_text: Established in each of those [identities], one should always worship <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> and <s>Hari</s>. (GGS 108)
The practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>), meditating constantly, dwelling in the house of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s beloved,

children.text: tad ājñā-pālako bhūtvā kāleṣv aṣṭasu sevate || 109 ||
children.translated_text: having become an executor of her commands, serves during the eight periods [of the day]. (GGS 109)
One should [visualize] oneself in the form of a companion of the <s>sakhīs</s>, filled with contemplation,
adorned with the grace of command, service, and supreme excellence,

children.text: tataś ca mañjarī-rūpān gurvādīn api saṃsmaret || 110 ||
children.translated_text: and then remember the <s>guru</s> and others in the form of <s>mañjarīs</s>. (GGS 110)

body.text: atha prātaḥ-pūrvāhna-līlāṃ smṛtvā madhyāhne saṅga-mitau rādhā-kṛṣṇau paraspara-saṅga-janita-nānā-sāttvika-vikāra-bhūṣitau lalitādi-priya-sakhī-vṛnda-sanarma-vāg-vilāsena janita-paramānandau nānā-rasa-vilāsa-cihnau sammagna-mānasau vihitāraṇya-līlau vṛndāraṇye sumahīruha-mūle yoga-pīṭhopari upaviṣṭau evambhūtau rādhā-kṛṣṇau saṃsmaret /
body.translated_text: Then, having remembered the morning and forenoon <s>līlā</s> (divine play), at midday, when <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are united, adorned with various <s>sāttvika</s> transformations born from their mutual meeting, experiencing supreme bliss through the playful, humorous conversation of <s>Lalitā</s> and other dear <s>sakhīs</s>, bearing the marks of the play of various <s>rasas</s>, with absorbed minds, engaged in the forest <s>līlā</s>, seated upon the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> at the root of a great tree in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>—one should remember <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in such a state.

children.translated_text: First, a lotus of six petals; outside that, one of eight petals;
outside that, one of ten petals, accompanied by ten sub-petals. (GGS 111)
Its form is filled with the <s>rasa</s> of the divine play (<s>līlā</s>) of <s>Śrīmad Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
it shines, opened or closed according to their respective desires. (GGS 112)
Outside that are ramparts, and at the four directions, four gateways;
four corners on the six-petaled [lotus], with the eighteen-syllable <s>mantra</s> of the six-footed [bee]. (GGS 113)

body.translated_text: As in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (2-4):

children.translated_text: The thousand-petaled lotus called <s>Gokula</s> is the great abode;
its pericarp is that realm, born from the portion of the Infinite. (GGS 114)
The pericarp is the great <s>yantra</s>, hexagonal, with a diamond peg,
six-limbed, the seat of the six-footed [bee], with <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. (GGS 115)
Established in the <s>rasa</s> of the great bliss of the bliss of love (<s>premānanda</s>),
in the form of light, combined with the <s>mantra</s> of the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (seed of desire). (GGS 116)

body.translated_text: Its filaments are the portions of that; its petals are [the abodes] of the <s>Śrīs</s> (goddesses of fortune). (GGS 117)
On such a <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>, one should remember <s>Śrī Śrī Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.translated_text: Now, the age, dress, and all other [aspects] of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇacandra</s>
are determined according to the <s>rasa-śāstras</s> (scriptures of aesthetic sentiment), as understood. (GGS 118)

body.translated_text: (<s>Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s> 2.1.308-9):
Age is threefold: <s>kaumāra</s> (childhood), <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (boyhood), and <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence). (GGS 119)

children.translated_text: <s>Kaumāra</s> extends to the end of the fifth year; <s>paugaṇḍa</s> up to the tenth;

children.text: āṣoḍaśāc ca kaiśoraṃ yauvanaṃ syāt tataḥ param || 120 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>kaiśora</s> up to sixteen; after that is <s>yauvana</s> (youth). (GGS 120)
Each of <s>kaumāra</s> and the rest is threefold, divided into beginning, middle, and end;
each division is declared to be one year plus eight months. (GGS 121)

body.text:
tad yathā--ādya-kaumāram aṣṭa-māsādhikam eka-varṣam evaṃ madhya-kaumāram, evaṃ ca śeṣa-kaumāram; evaṃ pañcama-varṣa-paryantaṃ kaumāraṃ jñeyam /
ādya-paugaṇḍam aṣṭa-māsādhikam eka-varṣam; evaṃ madhya-paugaṇḍam; evaṃ ca śeṣa-paugaṇḍam; evaṃ ca krameṇa ṣaṣṭha-varṣam ārabhya daśa-varṣa-paryantaṃ paugaṇḍaṃ jñeyam /
ādya-kaiśoraṃ sārdha-dina-dvayottaraikādaśa-māsādhikam eka-varṣam; evaṃ madhya-kaiśoram; evaṃ śeṣa-kaiśoram; krameṇaikādaśa-varṣam ārabhya pañca-daśa-varṣa-nava-māsa-sārdha-sapta-dina-paryantaṃ kaiśoraṃ jñeyam /
body.translated_text: That is: early <s>kaumāra</s> is one year plus eight months; likewise middle <s>kaumāra</s>, and likewise final <s>kaumāra</s>; thus <s>kaumāra</s> should be known as extending to the end of the fifth year. Early <s>paugaṇḍa</s> is one year plus eight months; likewise middle <s>paugaṇḍa</s>; likewise final <s>paugaṇḍa</s>; thus <s>paugaṇḍa</s> should be known as spanning from the sixth year to the end of the tenth year. Early <s>kaiśora</s> is one year plus eleven months plus two-and-a-half days; likewise middle <s>kaiśora</s>; likewise final <s>kaiśora</s>; thus <s>kaiśora</s> should be known as spanning from the eleventh year to the fifteenth year, nine months, and seven-and-a-half days.

body.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇasya vraja-līlā--tatra śrī-kṛṣṇasya vraja-līlā pañca-dinottara-ṣaḍ-māsādhika-daśa-varṣīyā jñeyā (10-6-5) atha ca (BhP 3.2.26)--
body.translated_text: Now <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>Vraja-līlā</s>: <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>Vraja-līlā</s> should be known as lasting ten years, six months, and five days (10-6-5). And also (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 3.2.26):
For eleven years he dwelt there, his splendor hidden, together with <s>Bala[rāma]</s>. (GGS 122)

body.text: mahārāja-kumāratayā bhogātiśayena samṛddhyā varṣa-māsa-dinānāṃ sārdhatayā sārdha-sapta-dinottara-nava-māsādhika-pañca-daśa-varṣa-parimitaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇasya vayo jñeyam (15-9-7 1/2) /
body.translated_text: As the son of a great king, enriched with the abundance of enjoyments, [each] year, month, and day being counted as one-and-a-half, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s age should be known as fifteen years, nine months, and seven-and-a-half days (15-9-7½).

children.translated_text: In this very final <s>kaiśora</s>, in the [equivalent of the] sixteenth year, always

children.text: vraje vihāraṃ kurute śrīman nandasya nandanaḥ || 123 ||
children.translated_text: the glorious son of <s>Nanda</s> sports in <s>Vraja</s>. (GGS 123)
With flute in hand, dressed in yellow, of the radiance of an <s>indranīla</s> sapphire,
adorned with the splendor of the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem at his throat, decorated with peacock feathers, (GGS 124)
his chest shining with a garland of <s>guñjā</s> berries, resplendent with a jeweled necklace,
wearing a forest garland (<s>vanamālā</s>), his throat glowing with a golden pendant (<s>niṣka</s>), (GGS 125)
his chest resplendent with a golden line (<s>Śrīvatsa</s>) on the left side,
his chest shining with the <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland, a pearl of elephant-pearl adorning his nose, (GGS 126)
resplendent with makara-shaped earrings (<s>kuṇḍalas</s>) on both ears,
with jeweled bracelets on his hands, wearing a <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) <s>tilaka</s>, (GGS 127)
with a waist-belt of tinkling bells, with jeweled anklets on his feet,
<s>mālatī</s>, <s>mallikā</s>, <s>jāti</s>, <s>yūthī</s>, <s>ketakī</s>, <s>campaka</s>, (GGS 128)
<s>nāgakeśara</s> and other flower garlands beautifully adorning him—
thus dressed, the glorious son of <s>Nanda</s> is to be meditated upon. (GGS 129)
His horn is placed at the side of his left belly, within the waist-knot;
on the right, likewise, he holds a flute (<s>muralī</s>) adorned with jewels.
With his left hand he holds a straight, light, yellow-colored staff;
the lotus-eyed one waves a play-lotus with his right hand. (GGS 130)
Of this very <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s>, there are three pure mantras,
considered accomplished, bestowing the perfection of true loving devotion (<s>sat-prema-bhakti</s>) to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. (GGS 131)

body.translated_text: First, the extraction of the mantra, as in the <s>Sanat-kumāra-saṃhitā</s>:

children.translated_text: "<s>Hare Kṛṣṇa</s>" repeated twice,
then "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" likewise, and "<s>Hare</s>";
"<s>Hare Rāma</s>" likewise "<s>Rāma</s>",
and likewise "<s>Hare</s>"—this is the <s>manu</s> (mantra). (GGS 132)

children.text: hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare /
children.translated_text: <s>Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare</s>;

children.text: hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare || 133 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hare Rāma Hare Rāma Rāma Rāma Hare Hare</s>. (GGS 133)

body.translated_text: Its meditation, as stated there:

children.translated_text: One should meditate in the lovely <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
adorned with cowherds and cows,
in the shade of a <s>kadamba</s> tree,
cooled by the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>, (GGS 134)
on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> together with <s>Rādhā</s>,
absorbed in playing the flute,
charmingly bent in the triple-bend posture (<s>tribhaṅga</s>),
the God who bestows grace upon devotees. (GGS 135)
Especially this ten-syllabled [mantra]
bestows perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) by mere recitation.
The five limbs of this mantra
should be known by the wise. (GGS 136)

body.text: iti gautamīya-tantra-vākyāt rāga-mārge daśākṣara-gopāla-mantrasya prasiddhiḥ; tad-uddhāro likhyate, sa yathā gautamīya-tantre--
body.translated_text: From this statement of the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>, the renown of the ten-syllabled <s>Gopāla</s> mantra on the path of <s>rāga</s> (passionate devotion) [is established]; its extraction is written—as in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Extracting the syllable ending in 'kha' [i.e., kl],
combined with the thirteenth vowel [au → klīṃ],
the full syllable 'pa' with the fourth vowel [ī],
then ending in 'cha', ending in 'dha', these two likewise; (GGS 137)
the immortal syllable, a pair of 'ma' syllables,
combined with the face-circle [i.e., 'va'];
then 'bha' combined with the face-circle,
and the wind-syllable [ya] likewise. (GGS 138)
Combined with the seed and the power (<s>śakti</s>),
this mantra is declared.
Due to the secret nature of the seed,
it is called the ten-syllabled [mantra]. (GGS 139)
The <s>Brahma</s>-syllable combined with the fourth [vowel],
accompanied by two 'ma' syllables,
combined with <s>nāda</s> (resonance) and <s>bindu</s> (dot),
is declared as the seed of the universe (<s>jagad-bīja</s>). (GGS 140)
The 'śukra' syllable with the 'immortal' syllable
combined with the face-circle;
the sky [syllable 'ha'] with the face-circle—
this is declared as the supreme <s>śakti</s>. (GGS 141)

body.translated_text: The ten-syllabled mantra is: <s>Klīṃ gopījana-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.

body.text: aṣṭādaśākṣaro mantro, yathā --klīṃ kṛṣṇāya govindāya gopījana-vallabhāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: The eighteen-syllabled mantra is: <s>Klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya Govindāya gopījana-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.

children.translated_text: Of the beauty of a fully-bloomed blue lotus, with a moon-like face, fond of the peacock-feather crest,
bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, wearing the noble <s>Kaustubha</s>, beautiful in yellow garments,
his body worshipped by the lotus-eyes of the <s>gopīs</s>, surrounded by the host of cows and cowherds—
I worship <s>Govinda</s>, absorbed in playing the sweet flute, adorned with divine ornaments. (GGS 142)

body.translated_text: Now the extraction of the <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s> mantra, as in the <s>Svāyambhuvāgama</s>:

children.text: klīṃ tataḥ kāma-devāya vidmahe ca padaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Klīṃ</s>, then '<s>Kāmadevāya vidmahe</s>' is the [first] <s>pada</s>; then,

children.text: tataś ca puṣpa-bāṇāya dhīmahīti padaṃ tataḥ || 143 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Puṣpabāṇāya dhīmahi</s>' is the [second] <s>pada</s>; then, (GGS 143)

children.text: tatas tan no 'naṅga iti tataś caiva pracodayāt /
children.translated_text: '<s>Tan no 'naṅgaḥ</s>' and then '<s>pracodayāt</s>'—
this is the <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s>, the mother of twenty-four syllables. (GGS 144)

body.text: kāma-gāyatrī, yathā -klīṃ kāmadevāya vidmahe puṣpa-bāṇāya dhīmahi tan no 'naṅgaḥ pracodayāt /
body.translated_text: The <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s> is: <s>Klīṃ Kāmadevāya vidmahe Puṣpabāṇāya dhīmahi tan no 'naṅgaḥ pracodayāt</s>.

children.translated_text: Absorbed in play, subject to <s>Madana</s>'s power, his limbs embraced by <s>Rādhā</s>,
with furrowed brow, smiling beautifully, charming in his naive attire,
in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, in the bowers of ever-fresh creepers, filled with love,
the fully blissful <s>Mukunda</s> triumphs, playing his flute! (GGS 145)
As in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya Tantra</s>:
The <s>Devī</s> who is of the nature of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is <s>Rādhikā</s>, the supreme deity,
embodying all <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, the supreme radiance of all, the supreme enchantress. (GGS 146)
Through <s>Rādhā</s>, the Lord <s>Mādhava</s> [shines];
through <s>Mādhava</s> alone, <s>Rādhikā</s> [shines]—
they radiate among the people. (GGS 147)

body.translated_text: And in the <s>Ṛk-pariśiṣṭa</s>:

children.translated_text: And in the <s>Mātsya</s> [Purāṇa]:
In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> she is <s>Viśālākṣī</s>; in <s>Puruṣottama</s> she is <s>Vimalā</s>;

children.text: rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṃ tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane || 148 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s> is in <s>Dvāravatī</s>, while <s>Rādhā</s> is in the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. || 148 ||
And in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> (UN 4.5)--

children.text: yathā rādhā priyā viṣṇos tasyāḥ kuṇḍaṃ priyaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Rādhā</s> is dear to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so too is Her <s>kuṇḍa</s> (pond) dear to Him;
Among all the <s>gopīs</s>, She alone is the most beloved of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. || 149 ||
She is the very embodiment of <s>mahā-bhāva</s> (the highest ecstatic love), supremely excellent in Her qualities;
In the <s>Gopāla-uttara-tāpanī Upaniṣad</s>, She is celebrated as <s>Gāndharvā</s>. || 150 ||
The <s>hlādinī śakti</s> (pleasure potency), the supreme among all potencies—
She is the embodiment of the essence of that potency; thus it is established in the <s>Tantras</s>. || 151 ||
She, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, is always of supremely beautiful form,
adorned with the sixteen <s>śṛṅgāras</s> (cosmetic decorations) and possessing twelve ornaments. || 152 ||

body.translated_text: Regarding Her supremely beautiful form, as stated in the words of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> (UN 4.8)--

children.translated_text: Your hair is beautifully curled, Your face has restless, long eyes,
Your chest bears firm, rounded breasts, and Your waist is slender;
With head gracefully bowed and arms extended, Your hands are lovely with jewel-like nails—
O <s>Rādhike</s>, this festival of beauty captivates the three worlds! || 153 ||

body.translated_text: Regarding Her being adorned with the sixteen <s>śṛṅgāras</s>, as stated (UN 4.9)--

children.translated_text: Bathed, wearing a garment resplendent with a jewel gleaming at the tip of Her nose, with sacred thread, hair braided,
with ear ornaments, body anointed with sandalwood, flowers adorning Her hair, wearing garlands, lotus in hand,
<s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) reddening Her lips, clusters of dots on Her chin, eyes lined with <s>kajjala</s> (collyrium), beautifully decorated,
<s>Rādhā</s>'s feet resplendent with <s>alakta</s> (lac-dye), adorned with a <s>tilaka</s> mark—thus She possesses the sixteen adornments. || 154 ||

body.translated_text: Regarding Her being endowed with twelve ornaments, as stated (UN 4.10)--

children.translated_text: A divine crest-jewel, a pair of earrings fashioned from gold, a waist-belt,
necklaces, pairs of bracelets and bangles, and throat ornaments and rings,
pearl necklaces resembling stars, armlets and anklets set with jewels,

children.text: stuṅgā pādāṅgurīya-cchavir iti ravibhir bhūṣaṇair bhāti rādhā || 155 ||
children.translated_text: and resplendent toe-rings—thus <s>Rādhā</s> shines with twelve ornaments! || 155 ||

body.text:
madhye vayasi kaiśora eva tasyāḥ sthitiḥ /
pūrvavad divasa-gaṇanayā viṃśati-dinottara-pañca-māsādhika-nava-varṣa-parimitaṃ madhya-kaiśoraṃ vayaḥ (9-5-20); rāja-kumārītvād bhogātiśayena samṛddhyā varṣa-māsa-dinānāṃ sārdhatayā pañca-daśa-dinottara-māsa-dvayādhika-caturdaśa-varṣa parimitaṃ vayo 'syāḥ jñeyam (14-2-15) /
body.translated_text: Her age is situated in the middle of <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence). As calculated previously by counting days, Her middle <s>kaiśora</s> age is measured as nine years, five months, and twenty days (9-5-20); because She is a princess, due to the abundance of enjoyment and prosperity, the years, months, and days being counted as one and a half times, Her age should be understood as fourteen years, two months, and fifteen days (14-2-15).

children.translated_text: Her disposition is that of <s>madīyatā</s> (possessiveness toward the beloved), and Her affection is of the <s>madhu</s> (honey-like) type;

children.text: mañjiṣṭhākhyo bhaved rāgaḥ samarthā kevalā ratiḥ || 156 ||
children.translated_text: Her attachment is called <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (deep crimson), and Her <s>rati</s> (love) is <s>samarthā</s> (fully capable) and <s>kevalā</s> (exclusive). || 156 ||

children.text: kandarpa-kautukaṃ kuñjaṃ gṛham asyās tu yāvaṭe /
children.translated_text: Her bower is called <s>Kandarpa-kautuka</s> (Cupid's Delight), and Her home is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>;

children.text: mātāsyāḥ kīrtidā proktā vṛṣabhānuḥ pitā smṛtaḥ || 157 ||
children.translated_text: Her mother is known as <s>Kīrtidā</s>, and Her father is remembered as <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>. || 157 ||

children.text: abhimanyuḥ patis tasyā durmukho devaraḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhimanyu</s> is Her husband, and <s>Durmukha</s> is known as Her brother-in-law;

children.text: jaṭilākhyā smṛtā śvaśrūr nanandā kuṭilā matā || 158 ||
children.translated_text: Her mother-in-law is known as <s>Jaṭilā</s>, and Her sister-in-law is considered to be <s>Kuṭilā</s>. || 158 ||

children.text: yathā syur nāyakāvasthā nikhilā eva mādhave /
children.translated_text: Just as all the states of the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero) are found in <s>Mādhava</s>,
so too all the states of the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) are generally considered to be present in <s>Rādhā</s>. || 159 ||
The companions of that Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> are considered to be of five kinds:

children.text: sakhyaś ca nitya-sakhyaś ca prāṇa-sakhyaś ca kāścana /
children.translated_text: <s>sakhīs</s> (ordinary friends), <s>nitya-sakhīs</s> (eternal friends), <s>prāṇa-sakhīs</s> (life-friends),
<s>priya-sakhīs</s> (dear friends), and <s>parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs</s> (most intimate friends)—thus they are renowned. || 160 ||
The <s>sakhīs</s> are enumerated as <s>Kusumikā</s>, <s>Vindhyā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, and others;
the <s>nitya-sakhīs</s> are <s>Kastūrī</s>, <s>Maṇi-mañjarikā</s>, and others. || 161 ||
The <s>prāṇa-sakhīs</s> are <s>Śaśimukhī</s>, <s>Vāsantī</s>, <s>Lāsikā</s>, and others;
these have mostly attained the very nature of the Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. || 162 ||
The <s>priya-sakhīs</s> are <s>Kuraṅgākṣī</s>, <s>Sumadhyā</s>, <s>Madanālasā</s>,
<s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Mādhurī</s>, <s>Mañju-keśī</s>, <s>Kandarpa-sundarī</s>,
<s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Mālatī</s>, <s>Kāma-latā</s>, <s>Śaśikalā</s>, and others. || 163 ||
The <s>parama-preṣṭha-sakhīs</s> (most beloved friends) are <s>Lalitā</s> along with <s>Viśākhā</s>,
<s>Citrā</s>, <s>Campakalatā</s>, <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>, <s>Indulekhā</s>,
<s>Raṅgadevī</s>, and <s>Sudevī</s>—these eight are the foremost of all groups. || 164 ||
<s>Lalitā</s> and the others, though possessing the qualification to be group leaders,
out of desire for the mood of their beloved <s>Rādhā</s> and others, adopted the disposition of friendship. || 165 ||

body.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>madīyatā-bhāva</s> (the mood of possessiveness) is as follows--

children.translated_text: "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is the very essence of <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s> (the erotic sentiment), is most dear to me"—

children.text: iti yaḥ prauḍha-nirbandho bhāvaḥ sa syān madīyatā || 166 ||
children.translated_text: this firm and mature conviction is known as <s>madīyatā</s> (possessiveness). || 166 ||

body.translated_text: An example is as follows--

children.translated_text: He whose lotus face is radiant with a peacock feather,
the flute-player, is the lord of my life—
where has He gone from here, leaving me?
Tell me, O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, You who know everything! || 167 ||
Even when He playfully reveals four arms,
<s>Hari</s> is made two-armed by the love of the Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. || 168 ||

body.translated_text: As stated (UN 5.7)--

children.translated_text: At the commencement of the <s>rāsa</s> (dance), when He hid in a bower, and the doe-eyed <s>gopīs</s>

children.text: rdṛṣṭaṃ gopayituṃ samuddhura-dhiyā yā suṣṭhu saṃdarśitā /
children.translated_text: spotted Him, He cleverly revealed Himself fully in order to conceal—

children.text: rādhāyāḥ praṇayasya hanta mahimā yasya śriyā rakṣituṃ
children.translated_text: Alas! Such is the greatness of <s>Rādhā</s>'s love, that in order to protect its glory,

children.text: sā śakyā prabhaviṣṇunāpi hariṇā nāsīc catur-bāhutā || 169 ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Hari</s>, though all-powerful, could not maintain His four-armed form! || 169 ||

body.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>madhu-sneha</s> (honey-like affection) is as follows (UN 14.93-94)--

children.translated_text: Possessing an abundance of <s>madīyatā</s> (possessiveness),
the affection for the beloved is called <s>madhu</s> (honey);
it is self-manifesting in sweetness,
a confluence of various <s>rasas</s> (flavors of love). || 170 ||
is called <s>madhu</s> (honey) due to its resemblance to honey. || 171 ||

body.translated_text: This affection, bearing the warmth of intoxicated joy,
An example is as follows (UN 14.95)--

children.text: rādhā snehamayena hanta racitā mādhurya-sāreṇa sā
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> is fashioned entirely of love, alas, with the very essence of sweetness—

children.text: saudhīva pratimā ghanāpy uru-guṇair bhāvoṣmaṇā vidrutā /
children.translated_text: like a statue in a palace, though solid, She is melted by the warmth of <s>bhāva</s> (ecstatic emotion) and Her abundant qualities;

children.text: yan-nāmany api dhāmani śravaṇayor yāti prasaṅgena me
children.translated_text: when even Her name or abode comes incidentally to my ears,
there arises at once an incomparable, intensely blissful forgetfulness of the entire world. || 172 ||

body.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>mañjiṣṭhā-rāga</s> (deep crimson attachment) is as follows (UN 14.139)--

children.translated_text: That which is irremovable and independent of anything else,
which always increases in splendor—
that is called <s>mañjiṣṭhā-rāga</s> (crimson attachment),
as exemplified by <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>. || 173 ||

body.translated_text: An example is as follows (UN 14.141)--

children.text: dhatte drāg anupādhi janma vidhinā kenāpi nākampate
children.translated_text: It arises swiftly without any external cause and is not shaken by anything whatsoever;

children.text: sūte 'ty āhita-sañcayair api rasaṃ te cen mitho vartmane /
children.translated_text: it produces <s>rasa</s> (relish) even through ever-increasing accumulated experiences—if You two are on the same path;
it accumulates a wealth of ever-growing, wonder-producing, exuberant joy—
this incomparable festival of the bond of <s>prema</s> (divine love) between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>! || 174 ||

body.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>samarthā rati</s> (fully capable love) is as follows (UN 14.52-53)--

children.translated_text: When the desire for union, arriving with a certain special intensity,

children.text: ratyā tādātmyam āpannā sā samartheti bhaṇyate || 175 ||
children.translated_text: attains identity with <s>rati</s> (love), that is called <s>samarthā</s> (fully capable). || 175 ||

children.text: sva-svarūpāt tadīyād vā jātā yat kiñcid anvayāt /
children.translated_text: Whether arising from one's own nature or from some connection with the beloved,
<s>samarthā rati</s> is considered to be devoid of even a trace of forgetfulness and most intense. || 176 ||

body.translated_text: An example is as follows (UN 14.54, 55, 57)--

children.text: prekṣyāśeṣe jagati madhurāṃ svāṃ vadhūṃ śaṅkayā te
children.translated_text: Seeing every sweet woman in the world as Your bride with suspicion,

children.text: tasyāḥ pārśve gurubhir abhitas tvat-prasaṅgo nyavāri /
children.translated_text: Her elders on all sides prevented any talk of You near Her;

children.text: śrutvā dūre tad api bhavataḥ sā tulā-koṭi-nādaṃ
children.translated_text: yet hearing from afar the sound of Your ankle-bells,

children.text: hā kṛṣṇety aśruta-caram api vyāharanty unmadāsīt || 177 ||
children.translated_text: She became mad, exclaiming 'Hā <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!'—a cry that knew no end. || 177 ||
Her love, which is the splendor that produces wonder through waves of the most astonishing divine pastimes,
is never separated from the special desire for union—

children.text: ity asyāṃ kṛṣṇa-saukhyārtham eva kevalam udyamaḥ || 178 ||
children.translated_text: thus Her sole endeavor is only for the happiness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. || 178 ||

children.text: iyam eva ratiḥ prauḍhā mahābhāva-daśāṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: This very <s>rati</s> (love), when it matures, attains the state of <s>mahā-bhāva</s> (supreme ecstasy),

children.text: yā mṛgyā syād vimuktānāṃ bhaktānāṃ ca varīyasām || 179 ||
children.translated_text: which is to be sought by the liberated ones and the greatest devotees. || 179 ||

body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</s>, Tenth Canto (10.47.58)--

children.translated_text: These cowherd women (<s>gopa-vadhūs</s>) are the supreme among embodied beings on earth,
who have attained fully matured love for <s>Govinda</s>, the Soul of all;

children.text: vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: that which the sages who fear material existence, and we ourselves, desire—
of what use are births as <s>Brahmā</s> compared to the relish of the infinite stories of the Lord? || 180 ||

body.translated_text: The extraction of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>'s <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Gaurī Tantra</s>--

children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> conjoined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>, then fire combined with the face-circle,
the fourth case ending with the wife of fire—this is the eight-syllabled <s>mantra</s> of <s>Rādhikā</s>. || 181 ||

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is as follows: <s>śrīṃ rāṃ rādhikāyai svāhā</s>.

body.text: gāyatrī yathā -śrī-rādhikāyai vidmahe, prema-rūpāyai dhīmahi, tan no rādhā pracodayāt /
body.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is as follows: We know <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>, we meditate upon Her whose form is <s>prema</s> (divine love); may <s>Rādhā</s> inspire us.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation form) is as stated there--

children.translated_text: Smiling, of the complexion of <s>śrī-kuṅkuma</s> (sacred saffron), with a veil arranged at the edge of Her brilliant reddish garment,
beautiful in Her attire, a youthful maiden with a lotus hanging from the crest of Her braided hair,
placing a betel-leaf on the lotus-face of <s>Hari</s> with the gesture of thumb and forefinger,

children.text: parṇaṃ karṇāyatākṣīṃ tri-jagati madhurāṃ rādhikām arcayāmi || 182 ||
children.translated_text: with eyes extending to Her ears—I worship <s>Rādhikā</s>, the sweetest in all three worlds! || 182 ||
Of the radiance of molten gold, with jasmine flowers bound in Her dark tresses,
with a face like the autumn moon, with restless eyes like dancing <s>cakorī</s> birds, || 183 ||
the moonlight of Her smile on Her <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips bestowing life upon the world,
adorned with a pearl necklace hanging upon Her beautiful jeweled breasts, || 184 ||
wearing a dark-blue garment on Her hips, decorated with a network of small bells,
wearing jeweled anklets fashioned from various gems, || 185 ||
Her every limb enchanting with complete loveliness, beautiful in every part of Her body,
always standing beside <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sole embodiment of love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
immersed in the ocean of blissful <s>rasa</s>—I take shelter of that youthful maiden in the forest. || 186 ||
Golden-complexioned, wearing red garments, beautiful, with lovely eyes and a sweetly smiling face,
dark-complexioned <s>Śyāmā</s>, the fulfiller of all desires of <s>Śyāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)—I take shelter of <s>Rādhikā</s> in the forest. || 187 ||
Without the grace of <s>Rādhā</s>, the attainment of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> does not occur;
therefore <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> should be remembered together as a united pair. || 188 ||

body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa</s>--

children.translated_text: "If you have faith in <s>prema-bhakti</s> (loving devotion), if you desire My grace,
then, O <s>Nārada</s>, become a worshipper of <s>Rādhā</s> with heartfelt devotion." || 189 ||

body.translated_text: And likewise in the <s>Nāradīya Purāṇa</s>--

children.text: satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ satyam eva punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Truly, truly, again truly, truly again and again—
without the grace of <s>Rādhā</s>, My grace does not exist." || 190 ||
By the compassion of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>, one may attain the company of Her <s>sakhīs</s> (female companions);
by the mercy of those <s>sakhīs</s>, one may obtain a feminine form. || 191 ||
There is a bower called <s>Anaṅga-sukhadā</s> (Giver of Cupid's Bliss) on the northern petal;
it should be known as being of lightning-like color, surrounded by various flowering trees. || 192 ||
The king of bowers in the north is called <s>Lalitānandada</s> (Giver of Lalitā's Bliss);
<s>Lalitā</s>, of the complexion of <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow orpiment), resides there eternally. || 193 ||
Wearing garments resembling peacock feathers, beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
she has attained the state of <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (an aggrieved heroine), always united in love with <s>Hari</s>. || 194 ||
Devoted to <s>candra-tāmbūla</s> (camphor-scented betel), adorned with divine ornaments,
her age is fourteen years, eight months, and twenty-seven days (14-8-27). || 195 ||

children.text: asyā vayaḥ-pramāṇaṃ yat pitā mātā viśokakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Such is the measure of her age; her father is <s>Viśokaka</s>,

children.text: śāradā ca patir yasyā bhairavākhyo mato budhaiḥ || 196 ||
children.translated_text: and her mother is <s>Śāradā</s>; her husband is known by the learned as <s>Bhairava</s>. || 196 ||
In the <s>Gaura-rasa</s> (the pastimes of <s>Gaura</s>/<s>Caitanya</s>), she has attained the identity of <s>Svarūpa Dāmodara</s>;

children.text: iyaṃ tu vāma-prakharā gṛham asyās tu yāvaṭe || 197 ||
children.translated_text: she is of the <s>vāma-prakharā</s> (left-wing, bold) temperament, and her home is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>. || 197 ||

body.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the aggrieved heroine) is as follows (UN 5.85-86)--

children.translated_text: She whose lover, having transgressed their appointed time, has enjoyed another woman

children.text: bhoga-lakṣmāṅkitaḥ prātar āgacchet sā hi khaṇḍitā /
children.translated_text: and comes in the morning bearing the marks of that enjoyment—she is called <s>khaṇḍitā</s>;
she is characterized by angry sighing, silence, and similar states. || 198 ||
Seeing the lord of <s>Vraja</s> at dawn with disheveled hair, His arms marked with earring-impressions,
His chest smeared with transferred saffron, and His garland wilted,

children.text: ghūrṇā-kuḍmalite dṛśau vraja-pater dṛṣṭvā prage śyāmalā
children.translated_text: His eyes half-closed with drowsiness—seeing this, <s>Śyāmalā</s>

children.text: citte rudra-guṇaṃ mukhe tu sumukhī bheje munīnāṃ vratam || 199 ||
children.translated_text: bore the fury of <s>Rudra</s> in her heart, but on her face, that fair-faced one adopted the vow of the sages (silence). || 199 ||

body.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>vāma-prakharā</s> (left-wing bold heroine) is as follows (UN 6.2-5)--

children.translated_text: Due to superiority in good fortune and other qualities, one is called <s>adhikā</s> (superior); due to equality, <s>samā</s> (equal);

children.text: laghutvāl laghur ity uktās tridhā gokula-subhruvaḥ || 200 ||
children.translated_text: due to being lesser, <s>laghu</s> (junior)—thus the beautiful-browed women of <s>Gokula</s> are of three kinds. || 200 ||

body.text: pratyekaṃ prakharā madhyā mṛdvī ceti punas tridhā || 201 ||
body.translated_text: Each of these is further divided into three: <s>prakharā</s> (bold), <s>madhyā</s> (moderate), and <s>mṛdvī</s> (gentle). || 201 ||

children.translated_text: She who speaks boldly and whose words are difficult to transgress is called <s>prakharā</s> (bold);

children.text: tad ūnatve bhaven mṛdvī madhyā tat-sāmyam āgatā || 202 ||
children.translated_text: when that quality is less, she is <s>mṛdvī</s> (gentle); when equal, she is <s>madhyā</s> (moderate). || 202 ||

body.translated_text: Regarding the <s>laghu-prakharā</s> (junior-bold) type (UN 8.31)--

body.text: sā laghu-prakharā dvedhā bhaved vāmātha dakṣiṇā || 203 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>laghu-prakharā</s> is of two kinds: <s>vāmā</s> (contrary) and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (compliant). || 203 ||
Regarding the <s>vāmā</s> (contrary) type (UN 8.32)--

children.text: māna-grahe sadodyuktā tac chaithilye ca kopanā /
children.translated_text: She who is always eager to maintain her <s>māna</s> (jealous pique), and who becomes angry when it subsides,
