children.text: abhedyā nāyake prāyaḥ krūrā vāmeti kīrtyate || 204 ||
children.translated_text: who is generally unyielding toward the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero) and harsh—she is called <s>vāmā</s> (contrary). || 204 ||
In this group, <s>Lalitā</s> and others are celebrated as <s>vāma-prakharā</s> (contrary and bold). || 205 ||

body.translated_text: An example of <s>vāma-prakharā</s> is as follows (UN 8.36)--

children.translated_text: "These doe-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s> number more than eighty-four <s>lakṣas</s> (8.4 million),
and it is proclaimed that each one belongs exclusively to You, her companion of equal age;

children.text: ihāpi bhuvi viśrutā priya-sakhī mahārghyety asau
children.translated_text: moreover, this dear friend is renowned throughout the earth as most precious—

children.text: kathaṃ tad api sāhasī śaṭha! jighṛkṣur enām asi || 206 ||
children.translated_text: how then, O rogue, are You so bold as to try to seize even her?" || 206 ||

body.translated_text: Her group is as follows (from <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā</s> 1.242)--

children.translated_text: <s>Ratnarekhā</s> (<s>Prabhā</s>), <s>Ratikalā</s>, <s>Subhadrā</s>, <s>Candra</s>(<s>bhadra</s>)<s>rekhikā</s>,

children.text: sumukhī ca dhaniṣṭhā ca kalahaṃsī kalāpinī || 207 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumukhī</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Kalahaṃsī</s>, and <s>Kalāpinī</s>.

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Sammohana Tantra</s>—

children.text: lakṣmī līlā ca lalitā ṅe tato vahni-nāyikā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Līlā</s>, and <s>Lalitā</s>, with the dative ending, then the consort of Fire (<s>svāhā</s>);
This is the eight-syllable great <s>mantra</s> of <s>Lalitā</s>, which bestows <s>rāga</s> (passionate attachment)."

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ Lāṃ Lalitāyai Svāhā</s>.
Her meditation, as stated in the same [text]—

children.translated_text: "I remember <s>Lalitā</s>, the dear friend of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>,
Whose body mocks the splendor of <s>gorocanā</s> (bright yellow pigment), beautifully dressed,
Wearing garments [adorned with] peacock feathers, resplendent with auspicious ornaments,
Delighting in the service of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) to the Son of the King of <s>Vraja</s>."
In the northeast petal there is a grove called <s>Ānanda</s>;
There resides <s>Śrī Viśākhā</s>, of cloud-like complexion, beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
She has attained the state of <s>svādhīna-bhartṛkā</s> (one whose husband is under her control) in relation to <s>Hari</s> always;
She is resplendent with garments and ornaments for service, golden-limbed, wearing star-patterned garments.
Her age is reckoned as: fortnights fourteen, days two, months fifteen [i.e., 14 years, 2 months, 15 days];

children.text: asyā vayaḥ pitā mātā pāvano dakṣiṇā kramāt || 212 ||
children.translated_text: Her father, mother, <s>Pāvana</s>, and <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> [are named] in order.

children.text: patir yasyā bāhukākhyo 'py asau gaura-rase punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Her husband is named <s>Bāhuka</s>; and in the <s>Gaura</s>-<s>rasa</s> (golden dispensation),
She became renowned as <s>Rāya Rāmānanda</s> in the age of <s>Kali</s>.

body.text: iyaṃ tv adhika-madhyā hi gṛham asyās tu yāvaṭe || 214 ||
body.translated_text: She is of the <s>adhika-madhyā</s> (superior-moderate) type; her home is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>.
The characteristics of <s>svādhīna-bhartṛkā</s> (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.91)—

children.translated_text: "She whose beloved is nearby and under her control is called <s>svādhīna-bhartṛkā</s>;
She engages in water-sports, forest-play, flower-gathering, and the like."

body.translated_text: Example, as follows (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.92)—

children.translated_text: "Joyfully painting incomparable leaf-designs on her full breasts,
Placing upon both her ears blue lotuses with honey-intoxicated bees,

children.text: sakhelaṃ dhammillopari ca kamalaṃ komalam asau
children.translated_text: And playfully [placing] a soft lotus atop her coiffure—
The Tamer of <s>Keśī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) long delights the untroubled <s>Rādhā</s>."
"In this group, <s>Viśākhā</s> and others are of the <s>adhika-madhyā</s> (superior-moderate) type."

body.translated_text: (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 8.19)—
Example of <s>adhika-madhyā</s>, as follows (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 8.17)—

children.translated_text: "Let the garland sent by the dear friend be offered
To <s>Dāmodara</s>; here let me gather flowers.
I am not to be hinted at, O clever <s>Caturikā</s>, [out of] error, O friend—

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ kadarthayati mām adhikaṃ yad eṣaḥ || 218 ||
children.translated_text: For this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> treats me with excessive disregard."

body.translated_text: Her group, as stated in the <s>Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā</s> (1.243)—

children.translated_text: <s>Mālatī</s>, <s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Candrarekhā</s>, and <s>Śubhānanā</s>,

children.text: kuñjarī hariṇī caiva surabhiś capalāpi ca || 219 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kuñjarī</s>, <s>Hariṇī</s>, <s>Surabhi</s>, and <s>Capalā</s>.

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s>—

children.text: vāg-bhavaḥ sauṃ tato ṅe 'ntā viśākhā vahni-jāyikā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Vāgbhava</s> (<s>Aiṃ</s>), <s>Sauṃ</s>, then ending in the dative, <s>Viśākhā</s>, with the consort of Fire;
This is the eight-syllable <s>mantra</s> of <s>Viśākhā</s>, which increases <s>prema</s> (divine love)."

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Aiṃ Sauṃ Viśākhāyai Svāhā</s>.
Her meditation, as stated in the same [text]—

children.translated_text: "I worship <s>Viśākhā</s>, whose body mocks rows of fine <s>campaka</s> flowers, of good character,
Wearing star-patterned garments, resplendent with various ornaments,
Engaged in the gift of garments and ornaments before <s>Śrī Nandanandana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),

children.text: dāne ratāṃ sukutukāṃ ca bhaje viśākhām || 221 ||
children.translated_text: Full of joyful eagerness."
In the eastern petal, there is a grove called <s>Padma-kiñjalka</s> (Lotus Filament);
<s>Śrī Citrā</s>, beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, is the mistress there.
She has attained the state of <s>abhisārikā</s> (one who goes out to meet her lover), endowed with passion for <s>Hari</s>;
Resplendent with garlands of clove, of saffron-colored complexion,
Wearing crystal-like garments, always endowed with wonderful qualities;
Her age is reckoned with the number of <s>Manus</s> [14] in days,

body.translated_text: With months equal to the number of <s>Ṛṣis</s> [7], and <s>Śakra</s>'s [14] years—that is, 14 years, 7 months, 14 days.

children.text: caturo 'syāḥ pitā prokto janany asyāś ca carccikā /
children.translated_text: Her father is said to be <s>Catura</s>; her mother is <s>Carccikā</s>;

children.text: patiḥ pīṭharakaś cāsyā asau gaura-rase punaḥ || 226 ||
children.translated_text: Her husband is <s>Pīṭharaka</s>; and in the <s>Gaura</s>-<s>rasa</s>,
She attained the identity of <s>Govindānanda</s> in the fourth age (<s>Kali</s>-<s>yuga</s>).

children.text: iyaṃ tv adhika-mṛdvī ca gṛham asyās tu yāvaṭe || 227 ||
children.translated_text: She is of the <s>adhika-mṛdvī</s> (superior-soft) type; her home is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>.

body.translated_text: The characteristics of <s>abhisārikā</s>, as stated in (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.71-72)—

children.translated_text: "She who sends for her beloved or who herself goes out to meet him—
She is the <s>abhisārikā</s>, [either] in moonlight or in darkness, dressed suitably for the journey."
"As if hidden within her own limbs out of modesty, with all ornaments silent,
With her veil drawn, accompanied by a single trusted friend, she should go to her beloved."

body.translated_text: Example, as follows: (1) of the moonlight <s>abhisārikā</s> (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.74)—

children.translated_text: "The moon displays its full orb; in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> it produces dense moonlight;

children.text: sāndrāṃ sundari nandano vraja-pates tvad vīthim udvīkṣate /
children.translated_text: O Beautiful One, the Son of the King of <s>Vraja</s> gazes at your path;
You are adorned with moon-white sandalwood and dressed in fine cloth—
Will you not set your lotus-beautiful pair of feet upon the path?"

body.translated_text: (2) Of the darkness <s>abhisārikā</s> (<s>Vidagdha-mādhava</s> 4.22, <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.75)—

children.translated_text: "O friend, in the <s>kadamba</s> grove, covered with the ink of darkness,
The blessed <s>abhisārikās</s> go to meet the Enemy of <s>Baka</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>);
But around you, lightning-hued [rays], indicating the radiance of your body,
Alas, alas! These break asunder the dense darkness, your enemy!"
"Here in this group, the <s>adhikā mṛdavas</s> (superior-soft) are <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Madhurikā</s>, and others."

body.translated_text: (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 8.21)—
Example of <s>adhika-mṛdvī</s>, as follows (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 8.20)—

children.text: darāpi na dṛg-arpitā sakhi śikhaṇḍa-cūḍe mayā
children.translated_text: "Not even a glance was cast by me, O friend, at the peacock-feather-crowned one;

children.text: prasīda bata mā kṛthā mayi vṛthā purobhāgitām /
children.translated_text: Be appeased! Do not in vain show partiality toward me;
With his dancing <s>makara</s>-earrings, he suddenly adopts a playful gait—

children.text: tanoty ayam adūrataḥ kim iha saṃvidheyaṃ mayā || 233 ||
children.translated_text: He approaches from not far away—what am I to do about it?"

body.translated_text: Her group, as stated in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā</s> (1.245)—

children.translated_text: <s>Rasālikā</s>, <s>Tilakinī</s>, <s>Śaurasenī</s>, <s>Sugandhikā</s>,
<s>Vāmanī</s>, <s>Vāmanayanā</s>, <s>Nāgarī</s>, and <s>Nāgavallikā</s>.

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]—

children.translated_text: "<s>Lakṣmī</s> (<s>Śrīṃ</s>), <s>Citrā</s>, ending in the dative, with the consort of Fire—six syllables;
This is the <s>mantra</s> of the one named <s>Citrikā</s>, the friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as declared."

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ Citrāyai Svāhā</s>.
Her meditation, as stated in the same [text]—

children.translated_text: "I constantly remember <s>Citrā</s>, of saffron complexion,
Endowed with wonderful qualities, with a face beautiful with smiles,
Wearing crystal-like garments, engaged before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
In the offering of garlands of clove."
In the southeastern petal, in a grove of golden hue named <s>Pūrṇendu</s> (Full Moon),
<s>Śrī Indulekhā</s> resides, with limbs the color of <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment, yellow).
She wears garments radiant like pomegranate blossoms, beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
She has attained the state of <s>proṣita-bhartṛkā</s> (one whose beloved has gone abroad), passionate toward <s>Hari</s>.
She is resplendent in the service of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar, food offerings) to the Son of <s>Nanda</s>;
Her age is acknowledged in all scriptures [as follows]:
She is of the <s>vāma-prakharā</s> (contrary-sharp) type; she serves with a <s>cāmara</s> (fan) before <s>Hari</s>.

body.translated_text: With ten-and-a-half days, two months, and <s>Manu</s>'s [14] years [i.e., 14 years, 2 months, 10½ days];

body.text: gṛham asyās tu yāvaṭe pitā sāgara-saṃjñakaḥ || 241 ||
body.translated_text: Her home is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>; her father is named <s>Sāgara</s>.

children.text: asyā mātā bhaved velā patir asyās tu durbalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Her mother is <s>Velā</s>; her husband is <s>Durbala</s>;
In the <s>Gaura</s>-<s>rasa</s>, she became known as <s>Vasu Rāmānanda</s>.

body.translated_text: The characteristics of <s>proṣita-bhartṛkā</s>, as stated in (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.89)—

children.translated_text: "When the beloved has gone to a distant land, she is called <s>proṣita-bhartṛkā</s>;
Recounting the beloved's [qualities], wretchedness, emaciation, sleeplessness,
Neglect [of appearance], restlessness, stupor, anxiety—these are considered [her symptoms]."

body.translated_text: Example, as follows (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.90)—

children.translated_text: "The playful Enemy of <s>Madhu</s> dwells freely in <s>Mathurā</s>;
Spring intensifies anguish from all sides at every step;
Alas, this accursed enemy [spring] creates obstacles to my desired endeavor—

children.text: vidhatte pratyūhaṃ kim iha bhavitā hanta śaraṇam || 244 ||
children.translated_text: Who will be my refuge? Alas!"

body.text: vāma-prakharā-lakṣaṇodāharaṇe tūkte; asyā yūtho yathā śrī-kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikāyām (1.247)--
body.translated_text: The characteristics and examples of <s>vāma-prakharā</s> have been stated; her group, as stated in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā</s> (1.247)—

children.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgabhadrā</s>, <s>Citralekhā</s>, <s>Suraṅgī</s>, <s>Raṅgavāṭikā</s>,
<s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Suvicitrāṅgī</s>, <s>Modinī</s>, and <s>Madanā</s>.

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Īśāna-saṃhitā</s>—

children.translated_text: "<s>Vāgbhava</s> (<s>Aiṃ</s>), then <s>Indulekhā</s>, in the dative, with the consort of Fire;
This eight-syllable <s>mantra</s> of <s>Indulekhā</s> is declared."

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Aiṃ Indulekhāyai Svāhā</s>.
Her meditation, as stated in the same [text]—

children.translated_text: "I worship the <s>sakhī</s> named <s>Indulekhikā</s>,
Whose body's luster is equal to orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>),
With garments radiant as blossoming pomegranate flowers,
Who places <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) in the mouth of <s>Mukunda</s>."
In the southern petal there is a grove named <s>Kāmalatā</s> (Creeper of Desire),
Supremely delightful, of a luster equal to heated <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
<s>Śrī Campakalatā</s> resides therein, beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
She has attained the state of <s>vāsaka-sajjā</s> (one who has decorated herself and her home in expectation of her lover), passionate toward <s>Hari</s>.
She is of the <s>vāma-madhyā</s> (contrary-moderate) type, of <s>campaka</s>-flower complexion, wearing <s>cātaka</s>-bird-colored garments;
Her service is the offering of gem-garlands and the waving of the <s>cāmara</s> fan.

body.translated_text: With thirteen-and-a-half days, conjoined with two months,
And <s>Manu</s>'s [14] years [i.e., 14 years, 2 months, 13½ days]—such is her age.

children.translated_text: Her mother is known as <s>Vāṭikā</s>; her father is named <s>Ārāma</s>;

children.text: asyāś ca bhartā caṇḍākhyas tathā gaura-rase hy asau /
children.translated_text: Her husband is called <s>Caṇḍa</s>; and in the <s>Gaura</s>-<s>rasa</s>,

children.text: śivānandatayā khyātim āgatā hi kalau yuge || 252 ||
children.translated_text: She became known as <s>Śivānanda</s> in the age of <s>Kali</s>.

body.translated_text: The characteristics of <s>vāsaka-sajjā</s>, as stated in (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.76-77)—

children.translated_text: "When the beloved is about to come to her abode, she who adorns

children.text: sajjī-karoti gehaṃ ca yā sā vāsaka-sajjikā || 253 ||
children.translated_text: Her own body and her house—she is called <s>vāsaka-sajjikā</s>."
"Her activities are: fantasizing about love-play, gazing at the path,
Amusing conversation with friends, frequently watching for the messenger, and so forth."

body.translated_text: Example, as follows (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.78)—

children.translated_text: "Having seen the bower for love-play, bright with its flower-bed,

children.text: vapuḥ sālaṅkāraṃ nijam api vilokya smita-mukhī /
children.translated_text: And her own adorned body, smiling—

children.text: muhur dhyāyaṃ dhyāyaṃ kim api hariṇā saṅgama-vidhiṃ
children.translated_text: Again and again meditating on some manner of union with <s>Hari</s>,
<s>Rādhā</s>'s mind became intoxicated with the madness of <s>Madana</s> (Eros), fully enraptured."

body.translated_text: The characteristics and examples of <s>vāma-prakharā</s> have been stated; her group, as stated in the <s>Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa</s> (1.244)—

children.translated_text: <s>Kuraṅgākṣī</s>, <s>Suracitā</s>, <s>Maṇḍalī</s>, <s>Maṇimaṇḍanā</s>,
<s>Caṇḍikā</s>, <s>Candralatikā</s>, <s>Kandukākṣī</s>, and <s>Sumandirā</s>.

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Gāruḍa</s> [Purāṇa]—

children.translated_text: "Beginning with <s>Campakalatā</s>, ending in the dative, with the consort of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (Fire);
This eight-lettered <s>mantra</s> of <s>Campakalatā</s> bestows <s>prema</s>."

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Campakalatāyai Svāhā</s>.
Her meditation, as stated in the same [text]—

children.translated_text: "I always worship the beautiful <s>Campakalatā</s>,
Whose luster equals rows of <s>campaka</s> flowers,
Wearing <s>cātaka</s>-bird-colored garments, beautifully adorned,
Holding aloft a <s>cāmara</s> fan with a jeweled garland."
In the southwestern petal, in a grove of dark color,
<s>Śrī Raṅgadevikā</s> dwells, in the [grove] named <s>Sukhadā</s> (Joy-giving), eternally beloved of <s>Śrī Hari</s>.
She is of lotus-filament complexion, wearing garments radiant like <s>jabā</s> (hibiscus) flowers;
She has attained the state of <s>utkaṇṭhitā</s> (one who longs eagerly), always passionate toward <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.
She is resplendent in the service of sandalwood [paste]; she is of the <s>vāma-madhyā</s> (contrary-moderate) type;

children.text: gṛham asyā yāvaṭe tu vayomānaṃ bhavet punaḥ || 261 ||
children.translated_text: Her home is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>; her age is [as follows]:
Her mother is said to be <s>Śrī Karuṇā</s>; her father is <s>Śrī Raṅgasāgara</s>.

body.translated_text: With four-and-a-half <s>Veda</s> [4] days, two months, and <s>Manu</s>'s [14] years [i.e., 14 years, 2 months, 4½ days];

children.text: patir vakrekṣaṇaḥ prokto hy asau gaura-rase punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Her husband is said to be <s>Vakrekṣaṇa</s>; and in the <s>Gaura</s>-<s>rasa</s>,
She became known as <s>Govindānanda Ghoṣa</s> in the age of <s>Kali</s>.

body.translated_text: The characteristics of <s>utkaṇṭhitā</s>, as stated in (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.79-80)—

children.text: anāgasi priyatame cirayaty utsukā tu yā /
children.translated_text: "When the innocent beloved tarries, she who is eager [to meet him]—
She is called <s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> (one longing in separation) by those who know the <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states)."

children.text: asyās tu ceṣṭā hṛt-tāpo vepathur hetu-tarkaṇam /
children.translated_text: "Her symptoms are: burning of the heart, trembling, conjecturing causes,
Restlessness, shedding tears, recounting her own condition, and the like."

body.translated_text: Example, as follows (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 5.81)—

children.text: sakhi kim abhavad baddho rādhā-kaṭākṣa-guṇair ayaṃ
children.translated_text: "O friend, has he been bound by the ropes of <s>Rādhā</s>'s sidelong glances?

children.text: samaram athavā kiṃ prārabdhaṃ surāribhir uddhuraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Or have the unruly enemies of the gods begun a battle?
Alas! On the eighth night of the dark fortnight, even though the moon has risen in the east,

children.text: vidhu-mukhi! na yan māṃ sasmāra vrajeśvara-nandanaḥ || 266 ||
children.translated_text: O moon-faced one! The Son of the King of <s>Vraja</s> has not remembered me!"

body.translated_text: The characteristics and examples of <s>vāma-madhyā</s> have been stated; her group, as stated in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa</s> (1.248)—

children.translated_text: <s>Kalakaṇṭhī</s>, <s>Śaśikalā</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Premamañjarī</s>,
<s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Madhurā</s>, <s>Kāmalatā</s>, and <s>Kandarpa-sundarī</s>.

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s>, as stated in the <s>Kiśorī Tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: "<s>Lakṣmī</s> (<s>Śrīṃ</s>), Fire, <s>Raṅgadevī</s>, in the dative, with the consort of Fire;
This eight-syllable <s>mantra</s> of <s>Raṅgadevī</s> bestows <s>rāga-bhakti</s> (passionate devotion)."

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>Śrīṃ Rāṃ Raṅgadevyai Svāhā</s>.
Her meditation, as stated in the same [text]—

children.translated_text: "Of complexion equal to the filament of a lotus—"
Adorned with garments resembling <s>jabā</s> (hibiscus) flowers,
Accompanied by the service of sandalwood paste, of the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>—
I worship <s>Raṅgadevī</s>, who participates in the <s>rāsa</s> dance. (GGS 269)
In the western petal there is a <s>kuñja</s> (bower) of crimson color, most beautiful,
Known by the name <s>Tuṅgavidyānandada</s> (giver of the bliss of <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>). (GGS 270)
<s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> always resides there, full of eagerness,
Having attained the state of <s>vipralabdhā</s> (deceived heroine), she is ever endowed with <s>rati</s> (love) for <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. (GGS 271)
Her radiance is resplendent with <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) enriched with moon[-white] and sandalwood,
Her ornaments and garments are pale; she is characterized as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (deferential) and <s>prakharā</s> (bold). (GGS 272)

children.text: medhāyāṃ pauṣkarājātā patir asyās tu bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: She was born in <s>Medhā</s> (a place in <s>Pauṣkara</s>); her husband is <s>Bāliśa</s>,
She is rich in service through dance, song, and the like; her home is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>. (GGS 273)

body.translated_text: Her age is fourteen years, two months, and twenty-two days (14-2-22). (GGS 274)

children.text: asyā vayaḥ-pramāṇaṃ syād asau gaura-rase punaḥ /
children.translated_text: This should be known as her measurement of age. In <s>Gaura-rasa</s> (the pastimes of <s>Gaura</s>),

children.text: vakreśvara iti khyātim āpannā hi kalau yuge || 275 ||
children.translated_text: She has become famous as <s>Vakreśvara</s> [Paṇḍita] in the age of <s>Kali</s>. (GGS 275)
The definition of <s>vipralabdhā</s> is as follows (UN 5.83-84)—
When, after making an appointment, her beloved (<s>jīvita-vallabha</s>) fails to arrive due to fate,
She who suffers anguish within is called <s>vipralabdhā</s> (deceived heroine) by the wise;
She experiences <s>nirveda</s> (dejection), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>kheda</s> (distress), tears, fainting, sighing, and the like. (GGS 276)

body.translated_text: An example is as follows—

children.translated_text: The moon attains the sky; [but] by the lord of <s>Indirā</s> (i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
O friend, we have been deceived!
What shall we do here? Instruct us with care,
Quickly!'—thus saying, the doe-eyed one fell into exhaustion. (GGS 277)

body.translated_text: The definition of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is as follows (UN 8.38, 42)—

children.translated_text: She who is unable to endure the insistence of <s>māna</s> (jealous anger), who speaks reasonably to her beloved,

children.text: sāmabhis tena bhedyā ca dakṣiṇā parikīrtitā || 278 ||
children.translated_text: And who can be won over by him through conciliatory words—she is known as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (the deferential heroine). (GGS 278)

body.translated_text: <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> and others here belong to the <s>dakṣiṇā-prakharā</s> (bold-deferential) type. (GGS 279)
An example is as follows (from <s>Śrī Gīta-Govinda</s> 9.10)—

children.text: snigdhe yat paruṣāsi yat praṇamati stabdhāsi yad rāgiṇi
children.translated_text: You who are harsh to one who is tender, who are rigid toward one who bows down, who toward a passionate one

children.text: dveṣaṃ yāsi yad unmukhe vimukhatāṃ yātāsi tasmin priye /
children.translated_text: Show hatred, who turn away from one who faces you eagerly, O beloved—

children.text: tad yuktaṃ viparīta-kāriṇi! tava śrīkhaṇḍa-carcā viṣaṃ
children.translated_text: It is fitting for you, O contrary one! For you, sandalwood paste is poison,

children.text: śītāṃśus tapano himaṃ hutavahaḥ krīḍā-mudo yātanāḥ || 280 ||
children.translated_text: The cool-rayed moon is the burning sun, snow is fire, and playful joys are torments! (GGS 280)

body.translated_text: Her group (<s>yūtha</s>) is as follows (from <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa</s> 1.246)—

children.translated_text: <s>Mañjumedhā</s>, <s>Sumadhurā</s>, <s>Sumadhyā</s>, <s>Madhurekṣaṇā</s>,
<s>Tanūmadhyā</s>, <s>Madhusyandā</s>, <s>Guṇacūḍā</s>, <s>Varāṅgadā</s>. (GGS 281)

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: Beginning with <s>Lakṣmī</s> [-bīja], <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s> in the fourth [case], ending with <s>svāhā</s> (the beloved of fire)—
This is declared to be the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>, consisting of eight syllables. (GGS 282)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>śrīṃ tuṅgavidyāyai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Beautiful with abundant moonstone and sandalwood, having the splendor of auspicious <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron),
Her body adorned with ornaments set with fine jewels, resplendent in red garments,
Accompanied by an array of beautiful songs, possessing many virtues, with the sound of the <s>ḍampha</s> (drum) indeed,

children.text: nṛtyantīṃ purato hare rasavatīṃ śrī-tuṅgavidyāṃ bhaje || 283 ||
children.translated_text: Dancing before <s>Hari</s>, full of <s>rasa</s>—I worship <s>Śrī Tuṅgavidyā</s>! (GGS 283)
In the northwestern petal there is a <s>kuñja</s> of green color,
Named <s>Vasanta-sukhada</s> (giver of the joy of spring); <s>Sudevī</s> always resides there. (GGS 284)
She has attained the state of <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (separated by quarrel), endowed with <s>rati</s> (love) in the home,
Her complexion is beautiful like lotus filaments, and her garments are like <s>jabā</s> (hibiscus) flowers. (GGS 285)

children.text: asau ca jala-sevāḍhyā vāmā prakharikā matā /
children.translated_text: She is rich in the service of water, and is considered <s>vāmā</s> (contrary) and <s>prakharā</s> (bold);
Her age is fourteen years, two months, and four days (14-2-4). (GGS 286)
This is the measure of her age; her abode is in <s>Yāvaṭa</s>;
Her mother is said to be <s>Karuṇā</s> and her father is <s>Raṅgasāgara</s>. (GGS 287)
She was married to the younger brother of <s>Vakrekṣaṇa</s>;
In <s>Gaura-rasa</s>, she has attained the identity known as <s>Śrī Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s>. (GGS 288)

body.translated_text: The definition of <s>kalahāntaritā</s> is as follows (UN 5.87)—

children.text: yā sakhīnāṃ puraḥ pāda-patitaṃ vallabhaṃ ruṣā /
children.translated_text: She who, when her beloved falls at her feet before her <s>sakhīs</s> (friends),

children.text: nirasya paścāt tapati kalahāntaritā hi sā /
children.translated_text: Rejects him in anger and afterward suffers remorse—she is indeed <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (separated by quarrel);
Her symptoms are lamentation, burning grief, languor, sighing, and the like. (GGS 289)

body.translated_text: An example is as follows (UN 5.88)—

children.text: srajaḥ kṣiptā dūre svayam upahṛtāḥ keśi-ripuṇā
children.translated_text: The garlands personally brought by the enemy of <s>Keśī</s> (i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) were thrown far away,
His loving words were not allowed even near the range of my ears;

children.text: namann eṣa kṣaunī-viluṭhita-śikhaṃ praikṣi na mayā
children.translated_text: As he bowed, his crest touching the ground, I did not even look at him—

children.text: manas tenedaṃ me sphuṭati puṭapākārpitam iva || 290 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this heart of mine now bursts as though placed in a kiln. (GGS 290)
The definition and example of <s>vāmā-prakharā</s> have already been stated. Her group (<s>yūtha</s>) is as follows (from <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa</s> 1.249)—
<s>Kāverī</s>, <s>Cārukavarī</s>, <s>Sukeśī</s>, <s>Mañjukeśikā</s>,
<s>Hārahirā</s>, <s>Hārakaṇṭhī</s>, <s>Hāravallī</s>, <s>Manoharā</s>. (GGS 291)

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Rudra-yāmala</s>—

children.text: dve vāg-bhave ramā ṅe 'ntā sudevī dahana-priyā /
children.translated_text: Two [syllables] from <s>Vāgbhava</s>, then <s>Ramā</s> [-bīja], ending with <s>ṅe</s>; <s>Sudevī</s> [in dative], ending with <s>svāhā</s> (the beloved of fire)—
This is declared to be the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Sudevī</s>, consisting of eight syllables, bestowing <s>prema-bhakti</s> (loving devotion). (GGS 292)

body.text: mantro yathā--aiṃ sauṃ śrīṃ sudevyai svāhā /
body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>aiṃ sauṃ śrīṃ sudevyai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Having a luster equal to lotus filaments, of beautiful disposition,
Wearing red garments, her face radiant with charming laughter,
Rich in the service of water before <s>Śrī Nandanandana</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>),
Endowed with an array of fine ornaments—I worship <s>Sudevī</s>! (GGS 293)
There is a <s>kuñja</s> named <s>Rūpollāsa</s> (splendor of beauty), to the north of <s>Lalitā</s>'s bower;
The ever-beautiful <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> always resides there. (GGS 294)
The foremost among the <s>priya-narma-sakhīs</s> (intimate humorous friends), the beautiful <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>,
Whose bodily beauty resembles <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow orpiment), who is fond of garments made of peacock feathers. (GGS 295)
Her age is thirteen and a half years (13-6); she has adopted the nature of <s>vāmā-madhyā</s> (moderately contrary);
The wise call her <s>Raṅgaṇa-mālikā</s>. (GGS 296)
She is one day younger than <s>Lavaṅga Mañjarī</s>;
In the age of <s>Kali</s>, in <s>Gaura-rasa</s>, she has attained the identity of <s>Rūpa Gosvāmī</s>. (GGS 297)

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: Conjoined with the <s>Śrī-bīja</s>, ending with <s>ṅe</s>, <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> [in dative]—
This eight-syllabled <s>mantra</s> of <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> is proclaimed. (GGS 298)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>śrīṃ rūpa-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Whose bodily luster puts <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow orpiment) to shame,
Wearing fine cloth resembling the hue of peacock plumes,
A maidservant of the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>—
I worship that <s>mañjarī</s> known as <s>Rūpa</s>! (GGS 299)
There is a <s>kuñja</s> named <s>Ratyambuja</s> (lotus of love), to the south of <s>Indulekhā</s>'s bower;
The beautiful <s>Rati Mañjarī</s> always resides there. (GGS 300)
Her garments are of <s>tārāvalī</s> (star-patterned) silk; her bodily complexion is like lightning;

children.text: dakṣiṇā mṛdvīkā khyātā tulasīti vadanti yām || 301 ||
children.translated_text: She is known as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (deferential) and <s>mṛdvī</s> (gentle), and they call her <s>Tulasī</s>. (GGS 301)
Her age is thirteen years and two months (13-2);
In <s>Gaura-rasa</s>, in the age of <s>Kali</s>, she has attained the identity known as <s>Śrī Raghunātha</s> [Dāsa Gosvāmī]. (GGS 302)

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: <s>Vahni</s> [-bīja] conjoined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>, accompanied by the head-circle (<s>mukha-vṛtta</s>),
Ending with <s>svāhā</s>, the <s>mañjarī</s> [in dative] ending with <s>ṅe</s>—this is the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Rati Mañjarī</s>. (GGS 303)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>rāṃ rati-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Wearing a pair of garments of <s>tārāvalī</s> (star-patterned) [silk],
With a bodily complexion equal to lightning,
Dwelling near <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>—
I worship that beautiful <s>Rati Mañjarī</s>! (GGS 304)
To the east of <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>'s bower, there is a <s>kuñja</s>,
Named <s>Lavaṅga-sukhada</s> (giver of the joy of cloves), beautiful and delightful to behold. (GGS 305)
<s>Lavaṅga Mañjarī</s> joyfully resides there always;
She is one day older than the <s>mañjarī</s> known as <s>Rūpa</s>. (GGS 306)
Her beauty is like rising lightning; she is draped in <s>tārāvalī</s> (star-patterned) cloth;
She is ever a giver of bliss to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (deferential), and has adopted the nature of <s>mṛdvī</s> (gentle). (GGS 307)
Her age is thirteen years, six months, and one day (13-6-1);
In <s>Gaura-rasa</s>, in the age of <s>Kali</s>, she is famous as <s>Śrī Sanātana</s> [Gosvāmī]. (GGS 308)

body.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: Conjoined with <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Līlā</s> [-bījas],
Ending with <s>ṅe</s>, <s>Lavaṅga Mañjarī</s> [in dative],
Ending with <s>svāhā</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Lavaṅga Mañjarī</s>
Is declared to consist of ten syllables. (GGS 309)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>śrīṃ lāṃ lavaṅga-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Whose beauty puts the splendor of lightning to shame,
Adorned with garments beautified by auspicious star-patterns,
Who delights the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>—
I devoutly worship that <s>Lavaṅga Mañjarī</s>! (GGS 310)
To the west of <s>Citrā</s>'s bower, there is a <s>kuñja</s> named <s>Rasānanda-prada</s> (giver of the bliss of <s>rasa</s>);
<s>Rasa Mañjarī</s> always resides there. (GGS 311)
She is celebrated as the very life-force (<s>jīvātu</s>) of <s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s>;
Her silk garments are like swan's wings, and she possesses the luster of a fully bloomed <s>campaka</s> flower. (GGS 312)
She is nearly equal to <s>Lavaṅga Mañjarī</s> in her wealth of virtues;
She has attained the highest dearness, being sheltered by <s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s>. (GGS 313)
She is skillful in arranging meetings (<s>sandhāna</s>) and expert in carrying messages (<s>dautya</s>);
She is thirteen years old (13), and is considered <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (deferential) and <s>mṛdvī</s> (gentle). (GGS 314)

body.translated_text: In the age of <s>Kali</s>, she has attained the identity of <s>Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa</s> [Gosvāmī]. (GGS 315)
The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: <s>Vahni</s> [-bīja] conjoined with the head-circle (<s>mukha-vṛtta</s>), accompanied by <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>,
Ending with <s>svāhā</s> and the dative case—this is indeed the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Rasa Mañjarī</s>. (GGS 316)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>rāṃ rasa-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Clad in garments beautiful as swan's wings,
Possessing the luster of a fully bloomed <s>campaka</s> flower,
Endowed with a wealth of beautiful form and virtues—
I worship <s>Rasa Mañjarī</s> for all time! (GGS 317)
To the northeast of the <s>Campakalatā</s> bower, there is a beautiful <s>kuñja</s>,
Named <s>Guṇānanda-prada</s> (giver of the bliss of virtues); <s>Guṇa Mañjarī</s> resides there. (GGS 318)
She is celebrated as one who desires the happiness of <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>;
Her silk garments are like rows of <s>jabā</s> (hibiscus) flowers, and she possesses the luster of a mass of lightning. (GGS 319)

children.text: kaniṣṭheyaṃ bhavet tasyās tulasyās tu tribhir dinaiḥ /
children.translated_text: She is younger than <s>Tulasī</s> (i.e., <s>Rati Mañjarī</s>) by three days;
She has adopted the disposition of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (deferential) and <s>prakharā</s> (bold), devoted to delighting <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. (GGS 320)
Her age is thirteen years, one month,
And twenty-seven days—thus it is declared (13-1-27). (GGS 321)

body.translated_text: In <s>Gaura-rasa</s>, in the age of <s>Kali</s>, she is famous as <s>Gopāla Bhaṭṭa</s> [Gosvāmī]. (GGS 322)
The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: <s>Gaṇeśa</s> [-bīja] enriched with the head-circle (<s>mukha-vṛtta</s>), accompanied by <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>,

children.text: ṅe 'ntā vahni-priyāntā ca mantro vai guṇa-mañjarī || 323 ||
children.translated_text: Ending with <s>ṅe</s> and <s>svāhā</s> (the beloved of fire)—this is indeed the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Guṇa Mañjarī</s>. (GGS 323)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>gāṃ guṇa-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Adorned with silk garments resembling <s>jabā</s> (hibiscus), with a bodily complexion like a row of lightning bolts,
Desiring the delight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s fragrance—I worship <s>Guṇa Mañjarī</s>! (GGS 324)
To the north of <s>Sudevī</s>'s bower, there is a <s>kuñja</s> named <s>Līlānanda-prada</s> (giver of the bliss of <s>līlā</s>);
The lovely <s>Mañjulālī Mañjarī</s> always resides there. (GGS 325)
She is nearly equal to <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> in her friendship and wealth of virtues;
Her silk garments are like rows of <s>jabā</s> (hibiscus) flowers, and her bodily complexion is like molten gold. (GGS 326)
Her name is <s>Līlā Mañjarī</s>; she has adopted the nature of <s>vāmā-madhyā</s> (moderately contrary);
Her age is thirteen and a half years plus seven days (13-6-7). (GGS 327)

body.translated_text: In the age of <s>Kali</s>, in <s>Gaura-rasa</s>, she has attained the identity of <s>Lokanātha Gosvāmī</s>. (GGS 328)
The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—

children.translated_text: Conjoined with <s>Lakṣmī</s> [-bīja], <s>Mañjulālī Mañjarī</s> [in dative], ending with <s>svāhā</s> (the wife of fire)—

children.text: caturthyantā bhaven mantro daśārṇaḥ khalu kathyate || 329 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>mantra</s> is declared to consist of ten syllables. (GGS 329)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>śrīṃ mañjulālī-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: Whose bodily luster is like refined molten gold, enchanting,
Wearing red garments, adorned with beautiful fine ornaments,
A maidservant of the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>—
I constantly worship that <s>Mañjulālī</s>! (GGS 330)
Named <s>Vilāsānanda-prada</s> (giver of the bliss of <s>vilāsa</s>); <s>Vilāsa Mañjarī</s> resides there. (GGS 331)

body.translated_text: To the southeast of the <s>Vaiśākha</s> bower, there is a most beautiful <s>kuñja</s>,

children.translated_text: <s>Vilāsa Mañjarī</s> has taken shelter of the friendship of <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>;

children.text: svakāntyā sadṛśīṃ cakre yā divyāṃ svarṇa-ketakīm || 332 ||
children.translated_text: By her own luster, she has made even the divine golden <s>ketakī</s> flower seem her equal. (GGS 332)

body.text:
cañcarīka-dukūleyaṃ vāmā mṛdvītvam āśritā
kaniṣṭhā rasa-mañjaryāś caturbhir divasair iyam (12-11-26) || 333 ||
body.translated_text: Her silk garments are like bees [dark-colored]; she has adopted the nature of <s>vāmā</s> (contrary) and <s>mṛdvī</s> (gentle); she is younger than <s>Rasa Mañjarī</s> by four days (12-11-26). (GGS 333)

body.text: jīva-gosvāmitāṃ prāptā kalau gaura-rase tv asau || 334 ||
body.translated_text: In the age of <s>Kali</s>, in <s>Gaura-rasa</s>, she has attained the identity of <s>Jīva Gosvāmī</s>. (GGS 334)

children.translated_text: The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, from the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s>—
With <s>Śrī</s> [-bīja] and <s>Pracetasa</s> [-bīja], accompanied by <s>nāda</s>, <s>bindu</s>, and the head-circle,
<s>Vilāsa Mañjarī</s> ending with <s>ṅe</s>, ending with <s>svāhā</s>—thus the <s>mantra</s> is proclaimed. (GGS 335)

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is: <s>śrīṃ vāṃ vilāsa-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.

children.translated_text: Whose body puts the golden <s>ketakī</s> flower to shame,
Whose garments put the luster of bees to shame,
Who serves at the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—
I worship the beautiful <s>Vilāsa Mañjarī</s>! (GGS 336)

body.translated_text: Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, from the same source—

children.translated_text: To the west of <s>Śrī Raṅgadevī</s>'s bower, in the southwestern direction, there is a <s>kuñja</s>;
She whose name means "giver of the joy of musk" — there resides <s>Kaustūrī-mañjarī</s>. || 337 ||
She wears garments like glass, and possesses the radiance of a body of pure gold,
her age is thirty years; she is of the <s>vāmā</s> (left/contrary) disposition, having taken shelter of gentleness. || 338 ||

body.translated_text: In the age of <s>Kali</s>, she attained [the form] known as <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Kavirāja</s> in the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic mood) of <s>Gaura</s>. || 339 ||
The extraction of her <s>mantra</s> is as follows, in the <s>Kiśorī-tantra</s> —

children.translated_text: Joined with the <s>śrī-bīja</s>, ending with '<s>ṅe</s>', [then] <s>Kaustūrī-mañjarī</s>,

children.text: svāhānta iti vai prokto navārṇa-mantra ucyate || 340 ||
children.translated_text: ending with <s>svāhā</s> — thus is declared the nine-syllabled <s>mantra</s>. || 340 ||

body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is as follows — <s>śrīṃ kastūrī-mañjaryai svāhā</s>.
Her <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, in the same text —

children.translated_text: She whose body has the luster of a pure golden lotus,
wearing beautiful and enchanting garments with the brilliance of glass,
dwelling near <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> —
I worship <s>Kaustūrī-mañjarikā</s>. || 341 ||
Now, one should meditate upon the two lords of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, situated at the center of the lotus filaments,
possessing the beauty of ten million <s>Kandarpas</s> (Cupids), surrounded by the dear <s>sakhīs</s> (female companions). || 342 ||
Endowed with the attire, age, and form previously described, supremely enchanting —
the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner), equipped with his <s>sādhanas</s> (spiritual practices), should contemplate [Them] in his <s>siddha-deha</s> (perfected spiritual body). || 343 ||

body.text:
tatrādau mañjarī-rūpān gurvādīn tu svīyān svīyān praṇāly-anusāreṇa saṃsmaret śrī-guru-parama-guru-krameṇeti tataḥ śrī-rādhikāṃ dhyāyet /
tataḥ śrī-nandanandanam /
body.translated_text: Therein, first one should contemplate one's own <s>guru</s> and others in the form of <s>mañjarīs</s>, each according to one's own <s>praṇālī</s> (lineage), in the order of <s>Śrī Guru</s>, <s>Parama-guru</s>, and so on. Then one should meditate upon <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>. Then upon <s>Śrī Nandanandana</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>).
Now the extraction of the <s>yugala-mantra</s> (divine couple's mantra) as stated in the <s>Sanat-kumāra-saṃhitā</s> —

children.translated_text: "<s>Gopījana-vallabha</s>" and then "<s>caraṇān</s>" in sequence,

children.text: śaraṇaṃ ca prapadye ca tata etat pada-dvayam || 344 ||
children.translated_text: then "<s>śaraṇaṃ</s>" and "<s>prapadye</s>" — thus these two words. || 344 ||
The <s>mantra</s> consisting of three words is declared to have sixteen syllables.

children.text: namo gopījanety uktvā vallabhābhyāṃ vadet tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having said "<s>namo gopījana</s>," one should then say "<s>vallabhābhyām</s>";
the <s>mantra</s> consisting of two words is said to have ten syllables. || 345 ||

body.text:
mantro yathā--gāṃ gopījana-vallabha-caraṇān śaraṇaṃ prapadye,
namo gopījana-vallabhābhyām /
body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is as follows — <s>gāṃ gopījana-vallabha-caraṇān śaraṇaṃ prapadye</s>, <s>namo gopījana-vallabhābhyām</s>.
Its <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is as follows, in the same text —

children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) of this <s>mantra</s>, O best of the twice-born:
wearing yellow garments, dark as a rain cloud, two-armed, wearing a garland of forest flowers, || 346 ||
with a peacock feather crown upon His head, His face radiant as ten million moons,
His eyes rolling [in ecstasy], wearing <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers as ear ornaments, || 347 ||
on all sides with sandalwood paste, and in the middle with a dot of saffron,
wearing a variegated <s>tilaka</s> on His forehead, displayed in a circular form, || 348 ||
resplendent with two earrings brilliant as the rising sun,
His cheeks gleaming like mirrors, radiant with tiny drops of perspiration, || 349 ||
with a playful sidelong glance cast upon His beloved's face, His eyebrows raised,
with a high, beautiful nose, a pearl glistening at its tip, || 350 ||
His lips like ripe <s>bimba</s> fruits, radiant with the moonlight of His teeth,
His arms adorned with <s>keyūras</s> (upper arm bracelets), <s>aṅgadas</s> (armlets), fine jeweled rings, and other ornaments, || 351 ||

children.text: vibhṛtaṃ muralīṃ vāme pāṇau padmaṃ tathottare /
children.translated_text: holding a flute in His left hand, and a lotus in the other,
His waist gleaming with a golden girdle, His feet shining with anklets, || 352 ||
restless with the rapture of amorous play, with darting glances,

children.text: hasantaṃ priyayā sārdhaṃ hāsayantaṃ ca tāṃ muhuḥ || 353 ||
children.translated_text: laughing together with His beloved, and making her laugh again and again. || 353 ||
Thus, at the base of the <s>kalpa-taru</s> (wish-fulfilling tree), upon a jeweled throne,

children.text: vṛndāraṇye smaret kṛṣṇaṃ saṃsthitaṃ priyayā saha || 354 ||
children.translated_text: one should contemplate <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s>), seated together with His beloved. || 354 ||

children.text: vāma-pārśve sthitāṃ tasya rādhikāṃ ca smaret tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then one should contemplate <s>Rādhikā</s>, standing at His left side,
wearing fine blue garments, Her radiance equal to molten gold, || 355 ||
Her limbs covered by the edge of Her garment, Her lotus face bearing a gentle smile,
Her restless eyes like dancing <s>cakorī</s> birds fixed upon Her beloved's face, || 356 ||
with Her thumb and forefinger, upon the lotus face of Her beloved,
placing a betel leaf (<s>nāga-vallī</s>) mixed with areca nut powder, || 357 ||
Her full, high breasts adorned with a radiant pearl necklace,
Her waist slender, Her hips broad, decorated with a network of small bells, || 358 ||
wearing jeweled ear ornaments, anklets, and jeweled toe rings,
Her limbs the essence of loveliness and charm, beautiful in every limb, || 359 ||
immersed in the nectar of bliss, serene, in the bloom of fresh youth.
And Her <s>sakhīs</s> (companions), O best of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, are equal to Her in age and qualities,
devoted to Her service — they should be visualized with <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), fans, and the like. || 360 ||
Beneath the <s>kalpa-druma</s> (wish-fulfilling tree) in the resplendent <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>,
seated upon a throne in a glorious jeweled pavilion,
<s>Śrīmad Rādhā</s> and <s>Śrīla Govinda-deva</s>,
served by Their dearest companions — I meditate upon Them. || 361 ||

body.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.translated_text: Thus the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) should contemplate in this sequence, in his <s>siddha-deha</s> (perfected body),
together with his <s>sādhana</s> (practice), the Lord and Lady of <s>Vraja</s> situated at the filaments of the lotus. || 362 ||
